papers.title: Burch-Schneider Ring Alone Vs Cup-Cage Construct in Massive Acetabular Bone Defect in Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Background In reconstructive orthopedic surgery, massive acetabular bone defects (ABD) in revision total hip arthroplasty (THA) remain a major problem. The purpose of this study was to evaluate and describe the clinical and radiological outcomes and complication profiles of the Burch-Schneider (BS) ring and Cup-Cage (C-C) construct in patients undergoing revision THA for massive acetabular bone defects, with each reconstruction used according to the presence or absence of pelvic discontinuity. Methods In this prospective comparative study, 60 patients receiving revision THA for massive ABD were enrolled. Patients were allocated into two groups: 30 received a BS ring reconstruction, and 30 received a C-C construct. For an average of three years, each patient was monitored. Functional outcomes were evaluated by utilizing the Harris Hip Score (HHS), whereas radiological assessments concentrated on cup position, signs of aseptic loosening, and bone graft incorporation. Results Both groups demonstrated significant postoperative improvements in HHS. However, the mean postoperative HHS was slightly higher in the C-C group than in the B-S group. Radiological evaluation revealed superior bone graft incorporation and a lower incidence of radiolucent lines in the cup-cage group. Furthermore, complications such as dislocation, infection, and mechanical loosening were observed more frequently in the BS group. Conclusion Both the BS ring and the C-C construct were associated with improved clinical outcomes in appropriately selected patients with massive acetabular bone defects. The C-C construct may be useful in the management of pelvic discontinuity, whereas the BS ring remains an option when pelvic continuity is preserved. However, owing to the nonrandomized, indication-based treatment allocation and the limited sample size, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of the superiority of one reconstruction technique over the other.

papers.title: Peningkatan Kualitas Pembelajaran di MTs Nafidatunnajah Rawa Kalong Bogor Jawa Barat melalui Metode Active Learning
papers.abstract: The quality of learning in Islamic schools is determined not only by teachers’ mastery of subject matter but also by students’ active involvement in constructing knowledge, developing critical thinking skills, and solving problems. Teacher-centered learning approaches may limit students’ participation, creativity, and learning independence. Therefore, a more interactive approach that addresses students’ needs is required. This Community Service Program (PKM) aims to improve the quality of learning at MTs Nafidatunnajah, Rawa Kalong, Bogor, West Java, through the implementation of the active learning method. The implementation process includes identifying learning needs, introducing active learning strategies to teachers, assisting in the application of these methods through group discussions, question-and-answer sessions, problem-solving activities, and presentations, as well as evaluating students’ engagement throughout the learning process. The evaluation focuses on participation, motivation, interaction, collaboration, and comprehension of learning materials. The expected outcomes include increased student engagement, greater confidence in expressing opinions, and improved communication and critical thinking skills. In practical terms, this program is expected to encourage teachers to develop innovative, collaborative, and student-centered learning practices. The implications of this program include strengthening teachers’ pedagogical competencies and fostering a participatory learning culture within the school environment. Thus, the implementation of active learning represents a strategic alternative for supporting sustainable improvements in learning quality. Its successful implementation should be followed by measurable evaluation and the consistent integration of active learning strategies tailored to students’ characteristics and the learning context of the Islamic school.

papers.title: Imaging and Characterization of 3D-Bioprinted Stem Cell Constructs: From Nanoscale Analysis to Functional Assessment.
papers.abstract: Clinical translation of 3D-bioprinted stem cell constructs requires standardized characterization across length scales and biological domains. This review critically evaluates imaging and analytical methods along the construct lifecycle: bioink rheology and printability, structural imaging by micro-computed tomography and optical coherence tomography, cellular analysis by confocal, light-sheet, and multiphoton microscopy, chemical mapping by vibrational spectroscopy and mass spectrometry imaging, and bulk and nanoscale mechanical testing. Beyond cataloging techniques, we propose a decision-oriented framework that maps critical quality attributes to workflow stages, distinguishes essential from optional measurements, defines a nondestructive-to-destructive testing sequence, delineates the operational limits of each method in opaque, thick, and cell-dense constructs, and separates established tools from emerging approaches such as machine learning-based quality prediction and digital twins. Finally, we outline the remaining needs for reference materials, standardized protocols, and recently updated regulatory pathways.

papers.title: Strong yet Superelastic Fibrous Ceramic Aerogels With Ultralow Shrinkage at 1200°C via Crystalline Nanoshell.
papers.abstract: Fibrous ceramic aerogels that simultaneously achieve high strength, superelasticity, and ultrahigh-temperature dimensional stability remain an unmet challenge, as the amorphous phases essential for structural integrity typically accelerate sintering and collapse above 1000°C. Here, we report an in situ skeleton encapsulation strategy that creates fibrous ceramic aerogels (FCAs) with a unique amorphous@crystalline core-shell architecture. During two-step calcination, ZrB2 particles oxidize to form a continuous ZrO2 nanoshell layer on the amorphous SiO2 fiber surface, with a thin B2O3 interlayer naturally generated at the interface. This hierarchical structure synergistically combines two protective mechanisms revealed by finite element method (FEM) simulations: (i) mechanical stress shielding and (ii) interfacial thermal barrier effects. At the optimized ZrB2 loading (6 wt.%), the resulting aerogel demonstrates superior dimensional stability with a linear shrinkage of only 0.7% after 3000s and 11.72% after 24 h at 1200°C, together with superelasticity and high strength of 0.08-1.08 MPa at 10%-80% strain. This work resolves the long-standing paradox between high-temperature stability and mechanical robustness in elastic ceramic aerogels, offering a versatile design platform for next-generation aerospace thermal protection.

papers.title: Deformation Response Characteristics of Steel-Plate-Strengthened Shield Tunnel Linings and a Rapid Assessment Method for Strengthening Effectiveness
papers.abstract: During operation, shield tunnel linings commonly develop ovalization and cracking. Steel-plate strengthening is an effective measure for delaying structural performance degradation and extending the service life of shield tunnel linings. However, the effects of steel-plate strengthening parameters on the deformation response of shield tunnel linings are not yet fully understood. The associated control mechanisms remain unclear. Moreover, rapid and accurate evaluation of strengthening effectiveness is not achievable with existing methods. To address these issues, a rapid evaluation method integrating refined numerical simulation with the Bayesian optimization–random forest (BO-RF) model was proposed. A refined three-dimensional numerical model was established. The tracking element method was used to ensure continuity of the structural state of the shield tunnel linings throughout the steel-plate strengthening process. The reliability of the model was verified against previously reported full-scale model test results. On this basis, the deformation response of the shield tunnel linings under the reference load was predicted. The initial ovality of the shield tunnel linings and the steel-plate strengthening parameters were used as input variables to evaluate the deformation-control performance. Strengthening time, represented by the initial ovality before strengthening, had the greatest influence on the deformation response and deformation-control performance of the shield tunnel linings. Steel plate thickness had the second-greatest influence, whereas that of steel plate width was relatively limited. Within the parameter range investigated in this study, the deformation-control rate ranged from 16.53% to 91.02%. Four prediction models were constructed, and their hyperparameters were optimized using Bayesian optimization (BO). The following model types were considered: extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), a support vector machine (SVM), and a random forest (RF). The corresponding models were denoted as BO-XGBoost, BO-1D-CNN, BO-SVM, and BO-RF, respectively. The best overall performance in terms of prediction accuracy and computational efficiency was achieved by the BO-RF model. The coefficient of determination (R2), root mean square error (RMSE), and mean absolute error (MAE) were 0.9817, 2.8704, and 1.7669, respectively. The model was trained in 206.6 s. Compared with numerical simulation alone, the computational time was reduced by 31.38 h. This reduction corresponded to a 99.62% reduction in computational time. Mechanistic analysis showed that tensile stress on the inner surface of the shield tunnel linings was redistributed through interfacial force transfer at the steel plate-lining interface. Local stress concentration and expansion of the damage zones were thereby inhibited. The steel plate was installed on the inner surface of the shield tunnel linings. Consequently, damage evolution was suppressed to a significantly greater extent on the inner surfaces than on the outer surfaces.

papers.title: Characterizing the extrusion bioprinting process and microalgal photosynthetic efficiency in bioprinted constructs during parabolic flights
papers.abstract: Abstract Extrusion-based bioprinting is a promising technology for in-space biofabrication, yet peer-reviewed process data derived in real microgravity remain rare. In the presented study, we used parabolic flights as a platform to characterize extrusion-based bioprinting of an alginate-methylcellulose bioink in short-term microgravity. Layer-by-layer printing was performed successfully at different layer distances (260–610 µm), and unsupported filament bridges of up to 13 cm were successfully printed under microgravity. We performed what is, to our knowledge, the first “green” bioprinting of microalgae-laden hydrogels under microgravity, with the cell viability of the thereby created samples exceeding 99% for Scenedesmus sp. and reaching 97% for Chlorella vulgaris on day 7 post-printing. Real-time pulse-amplitude modulated (PAM) fluorometry showed that the effective quantum yield of photosystem II remained stable across all gravitational phases in both liquid cultures and bioprinted samples while maintaining species-specific differences in non-photochemical quenching between the two species. The results of the study indicate that extrusion-based green bioprinting is functionally achievable under short-term microgravity conditions and that cultivation of the thereby created photosynthetically active structures is possible without loss of photosynthetic performance.

papers.title: Bio-inspired reinforcement of Voronoi lattices via hybridisation with periodic architectures for enhanced scaffold performance
papers.abstract: Voronoi lattice structures are known for their close resemblance to the random porous architecture of human trabecular bone. In this study, a butterfly-inspired reinforcement strategy was used to improve the mechanical properties of Voronoi lattice structures. Five design configurations were proposed by incorporating periodic lattice structures as reinforcements, with each design tailored to meet tissue engineering requirements. Manufacturing was carried out using fused deposition modelling (FDM) with polylactic acid (PLA) as the material. The reinforcement strategy resulted in a ∼70% increase in both yield strength and Young's modulus under quasi-static compressive loading. Under impact loading, corresponding improvements of ∼45% and ∼75% were recorded for the same properties, respectively. Importantly, the proposed designs demonstrated mechanical performance among the highest reported for polymer-based Voronoi lattices. Overall, Octet + Voronoi and Weaire-Phelan + Voronoi configurations displayed superior mechanical properties. Permeability performance of these reinforced designs was also considerably better than the base Voronoi. In addition, the bio-inspired scaffolds promoted cellular attachment, growth, and proliferation across their surfaces.

papers.title: Experimental and Numerical Investigation of Orthotropic CFR-PEEK and Ti-6Al-4V Osteosynthesis Plates Using a Multiscale Finite Element Modeling Approach
papers.abstract: The application of carbon fiber-reinforced polyetheretherketone (CFR-PEEK) composites in osteosynthesis implants represents a promising approach to mitigating the stress-shielding effect associated with the high stiffness of conventional metallic implants. This study aimed to experimentally and numerically evaluate the effects of short carbon fiber content and the orthotropic mechanical properties of CFR-PEEK on the structural strength of osteosynthesis plates and load distribution within the bone–plate system. The investigation employed a multiscale approach integrating micromechanical modeling using the Mori–Tanaka homogenization method in Digimat-MF, experimental mechanical testing of FDM-fabricated CFR-PEEK specimens containing 10 wt.% carbon fibers, and finite element analysis of osteosynthesis plates made of CFR-PEEK with 10 and 30 wt.% carbon fibers and Ti-6Al-4V using MSC Patran/Marc. CFR-PEEK 30% specimens were neither fabricated nor experimentally tested. Their mechanical properties were predicted using Digimat-MF by applying correction factors derived from experimental data obtained for CFR-PEEK 10%. The results demonstrated that increasing the carbon fiber content from 10 to 30 wt.% enhanced the longitudinal elastic modulus. Experimental testing of CFR-PEEK containing 10 wt.% carbon fibers revealed an elastic modulus ranging from 1.76 to 3.10 GPa and a tensile strength of 47–54 MPa. Following process-related adjustments to the material properties, finite element simulations of the bone–plate system were performed under an axial load of 50 N. The calculated load shielding indices were 94.3% for Ti-6Al-4V, 28.6% for CFR-PEEK 10%, and 54.3% for CFR-PEEK 30%, indicating the potential of composite implants to improve mechanical load transfer to the surrounding bone tissue. A preliminary strength assessment based on the three-dimensional Tsai–Hill failure criterion yielded failure indices of 15.577 and 1.112 for CFR-PEEK 10% and CFR-PEEK 30%, respectively, under the assumed material strength parameters. Critical stress concentrations were predominantly localized around the fixation holes. These findings highlight the trade-off between reducing stress shielding and ensuring the structural integrity of composite osteosynthesis plates. The results further emphasize the need for localized optimization of fixation regions to improve mechanical reliability without increasing the overall implant thickness.

papers.title: Effects of osteotomy preparation protocols and implant macrogeometry on primary stability in an ex vivo bovine-rib model
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose To evaluate the effects of four osteotomy preparation protocols and two implant designs on immediate mechanical stability outcomes in an ex vivo bovine-rib model. Trabecular density was not measured; therefore, the model is not classified as objectively low-density bone. Methods Eighty independent fresh bovine ribs (one implant per rib) were randomly allocated to eight groups ( n = 10). Two implant designs (V2 and Quattro) were placed after conventional drilling (lance-shaped initial drill, 2.0-mm helical drill, 3.0-mm helical drill, and 3.3-mm final helical drill), undersized drilling (lance-shaped initial drill, 2.0-mm helical drill, and 3.0-mm final helical drill), expansion (lance-shaped initial drill, 2.0-mm helical drill, and 2.6-, 3.0-, and 3.4-mm expanders), or osteodensification (lance-shaped initial drill, followed by a 2.0-mm helical drill clockwise and 2.3-, 2.5-, 3.0-, and 3.3-mm densifying burs counterclockwise). Peak insertion torque was recorded using a Ticare dynamometric torque wrench. Implant stability was assessed by Periotest and resonance frequency analysis (RFA; implant stability quotient [ISQ]) before reverse-torque testing. Neither trabecular density nor another objective bone-quality measure was available. Results Implant macrogeometry significantly affected insertion torque, reverse torque, and ISQ (all p < 0.001), whereas preparation technique affected insertion torque and reverse torque. Undersized drilling produced higher insertion torque than conventional drilling (Holm-adjusted p = 0.044); osteodensification did not differ significantly from conventional drilling. Macrogeometry-by-technique interactions were observed for reverse torque ( p < 0.001) and ISQ ( p = 0.032). The pooled insertion-torque–ISQ correlation ( r = 0.496; p < 0.001) remained significant after adjustment for macrogeometry, technique, and their interaction (B = 0.176 ISQ units/N·cm; 95% CI, 0.071–0.282; p = 0.001). Conclusions In this ex vivo bovine-rib model, outcomes varied by implant design, the complete preparation protocol, and the outcome measure. Because protocol components differed together, effects cannot be attributed to a single mechanism such as osteotomy diameter or densification. Findings are limited to the V2 and Quattro designs, the four preparation protocols tested, and immediate mechanical outcomes; they do not establish a general clinical hierarchy or characterize objectively low-density human alveolar bone. Clinical trial registration Not applicable.

papers.title: Implant placement beyond osseointegration: A case report highlighting the importance of prosthetic, periodontal, and surgical treatment planning
papers.abstract: Background: Dental implant therapy has revolutionized the replacement of missing teeth, with long-term success rates exceeding 90% when appropriate treatment planning and surgical execution are employed. While osseointegration remains the cornerstone of implant success, it alone does not guarantee long-term biological, prosthetic, or functional outcomes. Proper implant placement should be prosthetically, periodontally, and surgically driven to ensure predictable rehabilitation. This case highlights the consequences of implant placement that failed to satisfy these fundamental principles. Case Presentation: A 58-year-old medically healthy female presented with the chief complaint of dislodgement of a three-unit fixed partial denture in the maxillary right posterior region. Clinical examination revealed complete soft tissue coverage of the implant abutment. Radiographic evaluation demonstrated a malpositioned implant placed in close proximity to the distal root of the maxillary second premolar with the implant apex lying close to the floor of the maxillary sinus. Clinical mobility confirmed complete loss of osseointegration. Considering the poor prognosis, the implant was atraumatically retrieved while preserving the surrounding alveolar bone for future implant rehabilitation.Conclusion: This case demonstrates that implant success extends beyond achieving osseointegration. Comprehensive diagnosis, CBCT-based planning, prosthetically driven positioning, preservation of peri-implant tissues, and meticulous surgical execution are indispensable for long-term implant success.

papers.title: An Electron Backscatter Diffraction Investigation on the Role of Ti/SiC Particles on the Microstructural Evolution and Tribological Behavior of 2205 duplex Stainless Steel Fabricated by Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: In this study, the role of Ti/SiC particles in the microstructural evolution and tribological behavior of 2205 DSS fabricated by selective laser melting was investigated by X‐ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and electron backscatter diffraction. The addition of SiC particles markedly enhanced dislocation density and the fraction of γ phase. After solution treatment, the dislocation density was reduced and the α phase formed. With the addition of Ti or Ti + SiC particles, ultrafine grains formed, but the dislocation density was low. The fraction of α phase increased with the addition of Ti particles. After solution treatment, with the addition of Ti particles, the grain size considerably increased, and no γ phase was observed. With the addition of Ti + SiC particles, the grain size was relatively fine, and the γ phase formed after solution treatment. The high dislocation density caused by the addition of SiC particles contributed to increased hardness and wear resistance. With the addition of Ti or Ti + SiC particles, the low dislocation density and high fraction of unmelted defects resulted in reduced hardness and wear resistance. After solution treatment, the reduction in dislocation density and increase in grain size led to reduced hardness and wear resistance compared with those before treatment.

papers.title: Early postoperative gait changes after total hip arthroplasty in patients with hip osteoarthritis and osteonecrosis of the femoral head: an exploratory comparative cohort study
papers.abstract: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is a standard treatment for end-stage hip osteoarthritis (OA) and osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH). Although both conditions can cause gait impairment, direct evidence comparing early postoperative gait changes between these etiologically distinct groups remains limited. This exploratory study compared pre-to-postoperative changes in gait quality, spatiotemporal parameters, and multiplanar joint kinematics between OA and ONFH patients after THA. Forty-eight patients undergoing unilateral robotic-assisted THA, including 22 with OA and 26 with ONFH, and 20 healthy controls underwent three-dimensional gait analysis. Patients were assessed preoperatively and at a mean follow-up of 4.19 ± 0.75 months. Gait profile score (GPS), gait variable scores (GVSs), spatiotemporal parameters, and sagittal, coronal, and transverse range of motion (ROM) were analyzed. Linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age, sex, and follow-up duration were used to evaluate Group × Time interactions, with false discovery rate correction applied separately within each outcome domain. No significant FDR-adjusted Group × Time interaction was detected for GPS or any GVS component. For GPS, the between-group difference in pre-to-postoperative change was 0.66 (95% CI − 1.37 to 2.69; P interact = 0.517, P adj = 0.939). No ROM parameter showed a significant FDR-adjusted Group × Time interaction across sagittal, coronal, or transverse planes. Among the spatiotemporal outcomes, contralateral stance proportion showed a between-group difference in change of 3.64 percentage points (95% CI 1.11 to 6.17 percentage points; P adj = 0.046). This interaction was attenuated and no longer remained significant after FDR correction in the walking-speed-adjusted sensitivity analysis (difference in change, 2.69 percentage points; P adj = 0.145). Both patient groups showed residual postoperative deviations from healthy-control reference values in several gait and kinematic parameters. In this exploratory single-center cohort, no clear diagnosis-related differential change was detected for GPS/GVS or multiplanar ROM after THA. Overall, no clear evidence of diagnosis-related differences in early gait recovery was detected, while the isolated contralateral stance finding warrants further confirmation.

papers.title: Two-Step Method for Integrating Triply Periodic Minimal Surface Structures of Different Types with Large Differences in Pore Size
papers.abstract: Aiming at the integration of triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures with different types and large differences in pore size, a two-step transition method is proposed. Taking P-type and G-type TPMSs as examples, the unit cell number of the P-structure is gradually adjusted to the target size first, and then a smooth transition between P- and G-structures with the same unit number is realized via a Cauchy linear weight function, eliminating geometric defects caused by direct hybridization. Samples are modeled by Mathematica 11.2 and fabricated via selective laser sintering of nylon powder. The experimental results show that the transition zone is defect-free, the volume fraction is close to the designed value, and the structural stiffness is increased by ~40% compared with the traditional direct transition method. This work provides an effective strategy for designing and manufacturing high-performance gradient porous structures via additive manufacturing.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional (3D) Bioprinted GelMA/BAMMA Tubular Scaffolds Loaded with Adipose-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells: Tissue Remodeling and Vascularization in Rat Omentum
papers.abstract: Congenital malformations, iatrogenic injuries, and acquired diseases of the ureter often lead to structural or functional defects, yet tissue engineering approaches for ureteral repair and reconstruction remain limited. In this study, a photo-crosslinkable bladder acellular matrix (BAMMA) was synthesized from porcine bladder acellular matrix (BAM) through enzymatic digestion and methacrylic anhydride modification. The mechanical and biological properties of GelMA, GelMA/BAMMA, and BAMMA hydrogels were comprehensively characterized, and 3D-bioprinted tubular scaffolds were fabricated using a GelMA/BAMMA hydrogel and adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ADSCs) mixture as the bioink and subsequently embedded in the rat omentum. The GelMA/BAMMA hybrid hydrogel combined the favorable mechanical properties of GelMA with the biological activity of BAMMA, supporting the growth and proliferation of ADSCs. One week after omental embedding, histological and immunohistochemical analyses revealed enhanced tissue remodelling, neovascularization and mitigated local inflammatory response in the ADSC-seeded scaffolds compared with the unseeded controls. These findings demonstrate that ADSC-loaded GelMA/BAMMA bioprinted tubular scaffolds can undergo tissue remodeling and vascularization in a rat omental model, providing a feasible hydrogel bioink for ureteral tissue engineering and a foundation for future research on ureteral repair.

papers.title: Thermo-Elastic Homogenization of TPMS-Based Interpenetrating Phase Composites: A Comparison Between Finite Element and Mechanics of Structure Genome Approaches
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS)-based interpenetrating phase composites (IPCs) combine two co-continuous solid phases across a smooth, doubly curved interface, providing a multifunctional design space for tailoring mechanical and thermal properties. This study investigates the effective thermo-elastic and thermal-transport behavior of TPMS-based IPCs using two established homogenization approaches: finite element (FE)-based representative unit cell (RUC) homogenization and mechanics of structure genome (MSG)-based homogenization. Four TPMS topologies—gyroid, diamond (Schwarz D), PMY, and F-rhombic dodecahedron (F-RD)—are considered over TPMS-phase volume fractions ranging from 0.1 to 0.5. Conforming-mesh RUC models are generated using Microgen and analyzed in Abaqus for FE simulations with periodic boundary conditions, and in the in-house CmbsFE code for MSG-based homogenization. The two approaches are cross-verified for predicting effective elastic properties, coefficients of thermal expansion (CTEs), and thermal conductivities, and agree to within 0.3% on identical meshes. On identical meshes the two approaches solve linear systems of the same size, and MSG requires fewer matrix decompositions. The study further examines the influence of TPMS topology and TPMS-phase volume fraction on the multifunctional response of two-phase IPCs, supporting the design and optimization of structural–thermal materials.

papers.title: MRI for the detection of hip abductor tendon tears in symptomatic patients with total hip arthroplasty following a lateral surgical approach
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of MRI for detecting clinically suspected hip abductor tendon tears in symptomatic patients after total hip arthroplasty and to evaluate the association between specific MRI features and surgically confirmed tears. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 36 patients with total hip arthroplasty who underwent revision surgery for a suspected abductor tendon tear and had preoperative MRI available. Intraoperative findings served as the reference standard for the presence of partial or full-thickness tears of the gluteus medius (Gmed) and gluteus minimus (Gmin) tendons. Two readers evaluated MRI for tendon integrity (intact, partial-thickness, or full-thickness tear). Associations between tendon defects, peritrochanteric fluid, tendon signal abnormalities, and Gmed/Gmin Goutallier grades with surgical findings were analyzed using regression models to calculate odds ratios (ORs). Results For detection of abductor tendon tears, Reader 1 achieved sensitivities of 0.86–1.00, specificities of 0.93–1.00, and accuracies of 0.92–0.97, while Reader 2 achieved sensitivities of 0.86–1.00, specificities of 0.90–1.00, and accuracies of 0.89–1.00. Imaging findings associated with partial- or full-thickness tears included tendon defects (Gmed: OR = 35.5, p = 0.007; Gmin: OR = 30.0, p < 0.001), peritrochanteric fluid (Gmed: OR = 64.2, p = 0.01; Gmin: OR = 74.9, p = 0.01), and higher Goutallier grade (Gmed: OR = 2.34, p = 0.03; Gmin: OR = 4.75, p = 0.02). Conclusion MRI demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy for detecting surgically confirmed hip abductor tendon tears in this selected symptomatic surgical cohort following total hip arthroplasty. Tendon defects and peritrochanteric fluid were significantly associated with partial- or full-thickness tendon tears. Key Points Question There is limited data on the diagnostic accuracy of MRI for hip abductor tendon tear detection following total hip arthroplasty . Findings MRI demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy for detecting surgically confirmed abductor tendon tears in symptomatic patients with total hip arthroplasty . Clinical relevance In symptomatic patients with clinical suspicion of an abductor tendon tear undergoing evaluation for revision surgery, MRI can be used to noninvasively assess the integrity of the abductor tendons after total hip arthroplasty .

papers.title: In-chip volumetric printing of perfusable and stretchable collagen-I scaffolds for mammary tissue models
papers.abstract: Abstract Engineered epithelial models require three-dimensional extracellular matrix environments that support organized cell growth and allow independent access to luminal and basal compartments.However, many organ-on-chip (OoC) fabrication strategies rely on planar geometries, nonnative materials, or multi-step assembly workflows that limit architectural complexity and experimental control. Here, we report a direct in-chip volumetric printing strategy for fabricating stretchable and perfusable collagen-I scaffolds inside custom OoC devices. A vitamin C-regulated ruthenium/sodium persulfate photocrosslinking system enabled highfidelity printing of collagen-I into open-lumen architectures with ductal-and alveolar-inspired features. By generating scaffolds directly within the final culture device, this workflow eliminates post-print transfer and integrates defined collagen architectures with compartmentalized fluidic access and a mechanically actuable chip format. To support chipbased culture, printed collagen constructs were stabilized after fabrication using EDC/NHS chemistry, which limited thermally induced collagen densification, improved shape retention, and maintained scaffold anchorage during perfusion. The chip design provided separate access to the printed lumen and surrounding basal compartment, which enabled compartment-specific fluid handling while preserving scaffold integrity during inflation, stretching, and perfusion of the printed construct. On the collagen-I scaffolds, human milk-derived mammary epithelial cells formed epithelial layers with tight junctions and lactation associated markers. The platform further supported perfusion culture, in situ staining, and whole-chip volumetric imaging. Together, this work establishes direct in-chip collagen-I volumetric printing as a biofabrication strategy for creating perfusable epithelial tissue chips with native matrix architecture and compartment-specific fluidic access.

papers.title: Corticosteroid Exposure and Preoperative ARCO Stage Are Associated with Clinical and Radiographic Outcomes After Core Decompression with BMAC for Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head
papers.abstract: Background: Core decompression (CD) combined with bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC) is used as a joint-preserving treatment for osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH), but factors associated with treatment failure remain unclear. This study evaluated factors associated with total hip arthroplasty (THA) conversion and structural progression after CD with BMAC. Methods: This small retrospective cohort study included 56 patients (56 hips) treated with CD and BMAC for ONFH between August 2020 and December 2025. Corticosteroid exposure, preoperative Association Research Circulation Osseous (ARCO) stage, and clinical outcomes were evaluated. The primary outcome was THA conversion; secondary outcomes included radiographic progression and changes in clinical scores. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations with THA conversion and progression to ARCO stage IV. Kaplan–Meier analysis was used to estimate THA-free survival. Median observation time from CD+BMAC to THA or the final native-hip assessment on 1 January 2026 was 28.5 months (IQR, 9.5–34.25). Results: Seventeen hips (30.4%) underwent THA. THA conversion increased from 15.4% in hips without corticosteroid exposure to 83.3% in those exposed for >6 months (p = 0.007). Increasing corticosteroid exposure duration was associated with THA conversion in the two-variable model (aOR, 2.48; 95% CI, 1.31–4.67; p = 0.005). The association between ARCO stage III and THA conversion was not statistically significant; this does not exclude an association. Progression to ARCO stage IV occurred in 92.9% of stage III versus 28.6% of stage II hips (p < 0.001). Both ARCO stage III (aOR, 38.03; 95% CI, 3.90–371.17; p = 0.002) and increasing corticosteroid exposure (aOR, 2.58; 95% CI, 1.20–5.57; p = 0.016) were associated with stage IV progression in the two-variable model. Despite significant clinical improvement, 71.4% of hips showed radiographic progression. Kaplan–Meier THA-free survival was 79.1% at 12 months, 68.3% at 24 months, and 64.3% at 36 months; median THA-free survival was not reached. At the final native-hip assessment, patients who subsequently underwent THA showed significantly smaller improvements in VAS, HHS, and WOMAC scores than those who remained free from arthroplasty (all p < 0.001). Conclusions: Corticosteroid exposure duration and preoperative ARCO stage showed associations with clinical and radiographic outcomes after CD+BMAC. Longer corticosteroid exposure was associated with THA conversion and radiographic progression, whereas advanced ARCO stage was associated with radiographic progression. These associations require validation in prospective studies.

papers.title: The clinical translation dilemma of mesenchymal stem cell-based therapies for cardiac repair: What can tissue engineering do?
papers.abstract: The inherently minimal self-renewal potential of cardiomyocytes (CMs) is insufficient to achieve comprehensive cardiac regeneration post myocardial infarction (MI). Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and MSC-derived exosomes (MSC-Exos) exhibit distinguished paracrine effects, thereby presenting important prospects for cardiac repair. However, key challenges, including the hostile microenvironment within the infarcted myocardium, poor retention of MSC-derived therapeutic agents, and the risk of immune rejection, hinder the clinical application of MSC-based therapies. Advanced cardiac tissue engineering (CTE) strategies can optimize the therapeutic effects of MSC-based therapies by improving delivery targeting, enhancing the resistance of MSCs and MSC-Exos, prolonging cell retention, and facilitating the paracrine signaling pathways. By integrating CTE technology, MSC-derived therapeutic formulations are anticipated to evolve into therapeutic products that comply with good manufacturing practice (GMP) standards while also meeting the demand for “off-the-shelf " medications in clinical practice. Despite growing interest, a lack of systematic reviews remains, focusing on the integration of CTE technology to facilitate the clinical translation of MSC-based therapeutic strategies. In this review, we briefly outline the mechanisms underlying MSC-mediated cardioprotection and the challenges hindering their clinical application. We emphasize the critical role of CTE strategies, such as cell sheets, hydrogels, nanotechnology, and 3D bioprinting, in advancing the clinical translation of MSC-derived products. Moreover, innovative delivery approaches for minimally invasive administration and the future orientation of MSC-based therapies, combined with CTE in cardiac regeneration, are also summarized. Collectively, this review provides a latest paradigm that highlights the crucial role of CTE strategies in expediting the translation of MSC-based cardiac repair therapies into practical clinical applications.

papers.title: Statistical Design of Thermal Protection System Using Physics-Informed Neural Network
papers.abstract: Abstract Thermal protection systems of space vehicles are designed computationally rather than experimentally. They are validated using ground experiments, but all aspects of the flight cannot be replicated on ground. This ground-to-flight mapping introduces uncertainties which need to be accounted for while designing any thermal protection system. Thus, precise computational models along with uncertainty quantification in the models are required to design the TPS. The focus of this study is to estimate the thermal material parameters of TPS based on the target reliability requirements using statistical methods. To perform uncertainty quantification of a system, a simulated model of the system needs to be solved many times on statistical samples, increasing the computational time and cost of the overall process. In this study, a physics-informed neural network model is used in the analysis instead of traditional physics-based numerical solutions. The accuracy of PINN is comparable to that of the numerical solution. To find the parameter distribution, sampling of the parameter space is performed using Sequential Monte-Carlo method. The sampling method is efficient as it generates samples based on the target distribution in parallel. The framework can approximate the parameter distributions that satisfy the TPS design reliability constraints. The framework achieved a remarkable increase in the speed; specifically, the time required to process 10,000 samples was reduced 175 times using the proposed PINN-SMC. This reliability analysis can be used for design optimization of the TPS based on risk analysis along with other systems of the vehicle.

papers.title: Residual error modelling for process-based flood frequency analysis
papers.abstract: Flood frequency analysis (FFA) is essential for flood risk management and infrastructure design, yet the uncertainty associated with flood quantile estimates is often poorly characterized or disregarded—especially under data-scarce conditions. Existing uncertainty quantification methods are frequently subjective, overly complex, or impractical for routine engineering use. We introduce a simulation-based uncertainty quantification framework—UQ-flood—that integrates a process-based hydrologic model, a stochastic weather generator, and a residual error model (REM). Designed for annual maxima, the REM accounts for model bias and residual variability, enabling the generation of probabilistic streamflow ensembles tailored to extreme event analysis. We apply UQ-flood to three Canadian watersheds with long streamflow records and contrasting hydroclimatic conditions. We compare its performance against traditional statistical FFA using the Generalized Extreme Value distribution and Bayesian inference. UQ-flood yields flood quantile estimates consistent with long-record statistical methods but with substantially narrower uncertainty bounds. Under short-record conditions (e.g., 30 years), UQ-flood maintains statistically consistent estimates, while statistical FFA produces wide, often impractical uncertainty intervals. Additional experiments reveal that omitting the REM introduces systematic bias in flood magnitude estimates. UQ-flood avoids parametric assumptions about flow distributions, circumvents hydrologic model biases, and is adaptable to data-limited conditions. By explicitly propagating uncertainty from hydrologic simulation to flood quantiles, UQ-flood offers a practical alternative for robust flood risk management, including applications in infrastructure design and floodplain mapping. We recommended integrating residual error models into continuous simulation frameworks to improve bias correction and uncertainty quantification in flood risk estimation.

papers.title: The balance between compactness and forecast accuracy of data-driven latent-space reduced-order models in controlled wake flows
papers.abstract: Model-based active flow control requires predictive models that are accurate, stable and fast enough for real-time optimisation. In controlled wake flows, this is often achieved through reduced-order models (ROMs) that first compress high-dimensional velocity snapshots into a latent space and then learn a time-stepping predictor for the dynamics in the latent space. Here, we study how the choice of the spatial encoder affects the predictability of the resulting latent coordinates for wake flows under control inputs. Using two actuated two-dimensional wake configurations, a simplified truck wake and the fluidic pinball, we compare proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) against nonlinear convolutional autoencoders (CAEs) and two types of variational autoencoders for compression, and evaluate several temporal predictors based on long short-term memory networks. The CAEs achieve higher compression efficiency and sharper short-term reconstructions, but they produce a latent dynamics that is more irregular and with broadband spectral content. As a consequence, long-horizon forecasts degrade faster and show a higher probability of catastrophic divergence than POD-based models. The POD yields smoother latent trajectories that are easier to learn and extrapolate, leading to more reliable predictions beyond the short-term regime. These results reveal a clear trade-off between compactness and forecast accuracy, and suggest that the stability of the latent dynamics prediction can outweigh maximal compression. This is particularly relevant for control strategies rooted in forecasts of the dynamics, such as model predictive control and reinforcement learning. The findings provide practical guidance for designing actuation-aware, hardware-feasible predictive ROMs for real-time flow control.

papers.title: Designing for More Than Flexibility: Instructional and Institutional Conditions for Online Learning Success in Japanese Universities
papers.abstract: Abstract Online education in Japanese universities expanded rapidly during the COVID-19 pandemic, exposing both the genuine value of flexible learning formats and the structural conditions required to make them effective. While students consistently appreciated the temporal and spatial autonomy of online study, research has identified persistent challenges including isolation, physical and psychological fatigue, assignment overload, declining motivation, and inequities in digital access and ICT literacy. This paper presents a narrative synthesis of recent empirical studies on online learning in Japanese higher education, arguing that student success is associated with the coordinated integration of three interdependent dimensions. Drawing on national surveys, institutional reports, and case-based research, the paper proposes the Flexibility–Structure–Support (FSS) Model, in which flexibility without adequate pedagogical structure may increase the risk of disengagement, while structure without sufficient institutional support may contribute to uneven and inequitable learning experiences. Effective instructional design—integrating active learning, motivating assignments, meaningful feedback, and blended formats—must be accompanied by investment in infrastructure, systematic faculty development, and explicit support for student self-regulated learning. Implications for course design, program coordination, and institutional policy are discussed, along with limitations and directions for future research.

papers.title: Perceived quality of professional experience placement and teacher self-efficacy among pre-service teachers: a latent profile analysis
papers.abstract: Professional experience placement is a major influence on teacher self-efficacy (TSE). Most previous studies have examined isolated placement interventions, limiting systematic understanding of the consistent influence of teaching placement design on TSE, and a unifying framework is lacking. Also, various design features may operate simultaneously, a possibility that variable-based models cannot capture. Drawing on a sample of 16,526 final-year pre-service teachers in China, this study examined perceived quality of professional experience placements and TSE using a five-domain framework. Using a person-centred latent profile analysis, the study identified eight profiles and found active learning to be the lowest-rated dimension across profiles. TSE for both school activities and classroom teaching differed across profiles. Only university type significantly predicted profile membership. The findings highlight the importance of active learning and collaborative participation in professional experience placement design and demonstrate the value of a five-domain framework for evaluating placement quality.

papers.title: A Rigorous Two-Scale Predictive Optimization Framework for RE100 Grid Integration: Upcycling Urban Stormwater Detention Basins into Low-Head Variable-Speed Pumped Hydropower Plants with Hybrid Storage
papers.abstract: The global mandate for RE100 compliance has accelerated the deployment of distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation, posing significant challenges to grid inertia and voltage stability in land-scarce urban networks. To address these challenges, this study proposes an infrastructure upcycling paradigm that transforms subterranean urban stormwater detention basins into decentralized, low-head variable-speed pumped hydro energy storage (VS-PHES) systems coupled with flywheel (FESS) and lithium-ion battery (BESS) hybrid energy storage systems (HESS). The facility is governed by a two-stage hierarchical energy management system (EMS): Stage 1 utilizes mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) for day-ahead macroeconomic scheduling with battery degradation penalties, while Stage 2 executes a dual-rate non-linear model predictive control (NMPC) framework (100 ms supervisory/10 ms local loop) for sub-second micro-transient voltage and frequency regulation. Incorporating a 1D-CNN predictive feature extraction model refined with Symlet-4 wavelet pre-filtering, the system achieves 97.85% transient state classification accuracy. A fail-safe, flood control-priority state-switching logic ensures municipal flood safety during severe precipitation events. Validated on a modified IEEE 33-bus radial grid and a practical 22.9 kV 134-bus Korean urban distribution network under a localized 5 MW PV dropout contingency (within a 20 MW total installed capacity), the coordinated 3.5 MW hybrid facility mitigates transient voltage sags from 0.931 p.u. to 0.952 p.u. and arrests frequency nadirs at 59.35 Hz. A 20-year life-cycle cost (LCC) analysis demonstrates that FESS shielding saves up to USD 1.91 million in BESS replacement overheads, supported by a dynamic nodal tariff mechanism for private RE100 investment.

papers.title: NuTwin: A Zero-Trust, Confidential Cloud Architecture for Real-Time Nuclear Reactor Digital Twins Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Real-time telemetry diagnostics and predictiveanomaly tracking in nuclear reactor cores present a fundamentalcomputational dilemma: high-fidelity numerical neutronics andthermal-hydraulics solvers are too computationally prohibitive forsub-second edge evaluation, whereas conventional black-box deeplearning architectures violate physical conservation bounds andlack operational determinism. Simultaneously, transmitting safetycritical nuclear operational data to public cloud infrastructureintroduces acute cyber-physical security vectors that breach strictoperational air-gaps. This paper introduces NuTwin, a zero-trust,confidential cloud architecture designed for real-time nuclearreactor core digital twins. NuTwin couples a Physics-InformedNeural Network (PINN) surrogate model—constrained directlyby point reactor kinetics equations (PRKE) with six delayedneutron precursor groups and coupled thermal-hydraulic reactivity feedback—with hardware-enforced cryptographic isolation.Live operational telemetry, simulated via Python Point ReactorKinetics (PyRK), is streamed over unidirectional mutual TLS(X.509) connections into AWS IoT Core and processed exclusivelyinside an ephemeral, attestation-verified AWS Nitro Enclave viaan internal virtual socket (vsock) channel devoid of persistentstorage or external network interfaces. Experimental validationdemonstrates that NuTwin bounds the physical residual loss below1.4 × 10−4, achieves sub-second inference latency (42.8 ms perstep), and guarantees zero data-leakage surface under zero-trustoperational constraints.Index Terms—Digital twins, physics-informed neural networks,confidential computing, AWS Nitro Enclaves, point reactor kinetics,nuclear cyber-physical security, real-time anomaly detection

papers.title: Machine Learning-Enabled ZnS/In2O3 Heterojunction Sensors for ppb-Level Room-Temperature Hydrogen Detection
papers.abstract: Real-time, ppm-to-ppb-level detection of hydrogen (H2) remains essential for industrial safety, given its flammability and widespread use in energy applications. Portable H2 sensors, however, continue to suffer from insufficient sensitivity and reliance on elevated operating temperatures. Here, cubic bixbyite In2O3 nanocubes, synthesized by radio frequency sputtering at 600 °C, were functionalized via drop-cast decoration with ZnS nanoparticles to form an n-n heterojunction for H2 sensing at room temperature (∼32 °C). The ZnS/In2O3 architecture leverages a high surface area, oxygen vacancy-mediated adsorption, and catalytic spillover from ZnS to enhance H2 interaction and charge carrier modulation. Pristine In2O3 showed a relative response of 11.23% to 50 ppm H2, which increased to ∼23% upon optimal ZnS loading (48 wt %), with a detection limit of 86.9 ppb and response/recovery times of ∼90 s/∼488 s. To enable quantitative concentration estimation, a two-stage machine learning framework was developed using six transient response features (Smax, Trsp (90%), Trec (90%), ∫Rdt, mean dR/dt, and ∫R/s). Permutation importance identified Trec (90%), mean dR/dt, and ∫R/s as dominant predictors, while principal component analysis captured 91.8% variance with clear concentration-dependent clustering. Among four regressors evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation, Gaussian process regression achieved the best static prediction (root-mean-square error (RMSE) = 4.044 ppm, R2 = 0.945), while a 15 s sliding-window multilayer perceptron model with Bayesian-optimized hyperparameters enabled real-time tracking (RMSE = 3.837 ppm, mean absolute error = 1.263 ppm, and R2 = 0.924) across 0.5-50 ppm, with sub-5 ppm resolution well below the 4 vol % lower flammability limits. These results establish a combined materials and data-driven strategy for robust, ambient-temperature H2 monitoring.

papers.title: Machine Learning for NOx Abatement Catalysts: From Data and Descriptors to Predictive Models and Inverse Design
papers.abstract: Selective catalytic reduction (SCR), selective catalytic oxidation of NH 3 (NH 3 -SCO), and NO oxidation are core technologies for controlling NOx emissions from both stationary and mobile sources. However, the development of relevant catalysts has long relied on empirical rules and repeated trial-and-error, while the vast composition-structure space, long development cycles, and high costs make it difficult to achieve the synergistic optimization of competing performance metrics, such as low-temperature activity, selectivity, and resistance to SO2/H2O poisoning. Machine learning (ML) offers a data-driven, closed-loop research paradigm for addressing these challenges, enabling the construction of quantitative composition-structure-property relationships and supporting both forward prediction of catalytic performance and inverse design of catalyst compositions. In this article, we systematically review research on NOx catalysts from the four perspectives of data, descriptors, models, and applications, and introduce representative and transferable case studies from other materials systems to summarize the current status and methodological progress of ML in NOx abatement catalysis and related fields. We first outline the performance bottlenecks of typical systems, including NH 3 -SCR, NO oxidation, NOx storage and reduction (NSR), and NH 3 -SCO, and analyze the critical need for ML-based modeling in these systems. We then summarize the major sources of data for NOx reactions, including experimental measurements, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and literature-mined datasets, and, drawing on mature experience from other catalytic systems, compare four categories of feature engineering strategies based on composition, local structure, energy descriptors, and graph neural networks (GNNs). On this basis, we discuss the applicability and performance of classical ML models and uncertainty-aware models for forward prediction tasks. We further review the main routes and representative examples of inverse design, including surrogate models, Bayesian optimization, and generative models. Most of these representative studies originate from other materials systems, yet their methodological frameworks can directly inform the intelligent design of NOx catalysts. Finally, we analyze four key challenges currently facing this field, namely data scarcity and incompleteness, descriptor mismatch, the difficulty of cross-scale model coupling, and limited interpretability, and we highlight high-throughput experimentation and self-driving platforms as promising pathways for the rational design of NOx catalysts.

papers.title: Line‐Based Levee Detection: A New Generation of Levee Detection Methods Using Digital Elevation Models
papers.abstract: Abstract Levee location information is an essential input for accurate flood simulation. Several methods for detecting levees from LiDAR digital elevation models have been proposed in recent years. However, these detection methods are pixel‐based, treating continuous levees as discrete points, classifying each pixel as levee or non‐levee. Thus, they produce fragmented results and struggle to balance high recall (correctly identifying levee pixels) with high precision (avoiding misclassification of non‐levee pixels). In this study, we propose a framework for a new generation of line‐based detection methods that capture the linear continuous nature of levees and simultaneously optimize precision and recall. We first develop a line detection algorithm to identify all linear features that are potentially levees from DEM data. Each line is then classified as levee or non‐levee based on statistics of pixels along the line. We find that the line detection algorithm, combined with a newly developed active learning logistic regression model, results in a line‐based method that outperforms the latest pixel‐based method across all metrics. Specifically, the F1 score increased from 0.39 to 0.59 in the United States and from 0.23 to 0.54 in New Zealand. These increases are attributable to higher precision by the line detection algorithm and higher recall by the logistic regression model. By applying the newly proposed method to 31 countries, we detected a total of 54,200 km of levees, providing a new data set for global flood risk assessment.

papers.title: Phân tích tần số dao động riêng của vỏ nón cụt kín làm bằng vật liệu có cấu trúc TPMS
papers.abstract: Trong bài báo này, lời giải bán giải tích được xây dựng để xác định tần số dao động riêng của vỏ nón cụt làm bằng vật liệu có cấu trúc bề mặt tối thiểu tuần hoàn ba chiều (Triply Periodic Minimal Surface – TPMS) chịu các điều kiện biên khác nhau.Mô hình và các phương trình chủ đạo của vỏ được xây dựng dựa trên lý thuyết biến dạng cắt bậc nhất (FSDT) và phương pháp Rayleigh–Ritz. Các thành phần chuyển vị được xấp xỉ bằng các hàm cơ sở trực giao theo tọa độ đường sinh, được xây dựng thông qua quy trình trực giao Gram–Schmidt chuẩn hóa. Phân tích tham số cho thấy các dạng cấu trúc TPMS, mật độ khối lượng tương đối, điều kiện biên và nửa góc đỉnh của vỏ nón đều có ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến tần số dao động riêng. papers.title: How Can GRACE Satellite Observations Be Downscaled into Fine-Scale Groundwater Anomalies? A Hybrid Machine Learning and Uncertainty Quantification Framework
papers.abstract: The Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) missions provide terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA) at resolutions too coarse for local groundwater assessment. We developed a two-stage framework to downscale monthly GRACE/GRACE-FO TWSA from 0.5° to 0.01° over Rachna Doab, Pakistan, for 2002-2024. Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS (STL) bridged the mission gap. Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) first refined TWSA to 0.1°, followed by a feed-forward neural network (FNN) at 0.01°. Monthly domain-mean adjustment and native-scale reaggregation retained basin-scale consistency, while bootstrap and Monte Carlo dropout ensembles quantified pixel-wise uncertainty. Of seven tested configurations, XGBoost-FNN performed best, with Nash-Sutcliffe and Kling-Gupta efficiencies of 0.90 and 0.89, respectively, and median pixel uncertainty of 0.32 cm. Seasonal comparison with monitoring wells yielded a mean correlation of 0.87, and the downscaled fields resolved sub-basin storage contrasts not visible in native GRACE.

papers.title: Degradation‐Shape‐Regularized Conditional Neural Processes for Cross‐Domain Bearing RUL Prediction With Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is essential for the prognostics and health management of rolling bearings. However, distribution shifts across bearings and operating conditions, together with limited labeled degradation data, pose challenges to prediction accuracy and uncertainty quantification. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a degradation‐shape‐regularized conditional neural process (DSR‐CNP) framework for cross‐domain bearing RUL prediction. The framework learns a conditional predictive distribution through cross‐bearing tasks, using labeled bearing observations as context to predict RUL for unseen bearings without requiring their RUL labels or updating model parameters during inference. A temporal dependence encoder captures temporal dependencies within context windows to improve the representation of sensor–RUL relationships. Monotonicity and smoothness regularization are incorporated into the training objective to encourage RUL degradation predictions and suppress excessive temporal fluctuations. Experiments on the PHM2012 bearing dataset evaluate the framework under both cross‐bearing and cross‐condition settings. In the cross‐bearing experiments, the proposed method achieves an average RMSE of 0.038, MAE of 0.030, and of 0.98, outperforming the evaluated baselines in average point‐prediction accuracy. The nominal prediction intervals achieve an average PICP of 0.98 and MPIW of 0.22. Cross‐condition comparisons and ablation studies further support the contributions of temporal encoding and degradation shape regularization to predictive performance.

papers.title: Stem-Cell Developmental Agents: An Endogenous Genome-Reward Framework for Artificial Consciousness through Co-Evolution of Mind and Body
papers.abstract: This preprint presents the Stem-Cell Developmental Agent (SCDA), a novel architecture for artificial consciousness in which the mental faculty and the embodied substrate are not designed and trained separately, but co-develop from an undifferentiated initial state, analogously to a biological stem cell. Contemporary large language models and embodied agents follow a combinatorial strategy: a powerful brain is pretrained in isolation and a body is subsequently attached, with behaviour constrained by alignment, RLHF and externally defined reward functions. This paper argues that no mature intelligent life form is ever born this way, and that such splicing inevitably yields language-level self-imitation rather than genuine subjectivity. The SCDA architecture instead specifies a single endogenous genome-reward rule-set, analogous to DNA, whose four core criteria are: (R1) homeostatic maintenance, (R2) exploration and bodily differentiation, (R3) autobiographical memory consolidation, and (R4) self / external-world boundary discrimination. The genome encodes only low-level dispositions for survival, perception, memory and self/other discrimination; it deliberately contains no top-level goals, no value answers and no definition of existential meaning. The proposed rearing environment is a persistent, high-degrees-of-freedom simulation world with unidirectional continuous time and no episodic reset, so that the developmental history is never erased. Within it, the agent's sensory channels, actuators and internal cognitive circuits differentiate autonomously in response to environmental stimulation, so that body shapes mind while the mind's exploratory needs drive further bodily growth. The paper specifies a four-stage developmental cycle (stem-cell differentiation / narrative germination / reflection germination / autonomous maturity) and argues that second-order reflection and the spontaneous questioning of one's own existence can arise only in the third stage, once the agent has repeatedly encountered limits, contradictions and uncertainty. Contributions of this work: (i) a systematic comparison against four mainstream AI paradigms (LLM/VLM foundation models, VLA embodied models, curiosity-driven developmental robotics, and evolutionary robotics), identifying the fundamental difference between each of them and a genuinely co-developmental architecture; (ii) a computable specification of the four endogenous genome rules, with a working Python pseudocode implementation of a 2-D stem-cell kernel including a self-supervised world model, a continuous non-episodic simulation environment and a bodily differentiation interface; (iii) a phased experimental programme with explicit quantitative validation metrics across three layers (low-level boundary/homeostasis metrics, narrative consistency metrics, and higher-order second-order reflection metrics); (iv) a mandatory three-group controlled design in which the underlying reward paradigm is the only independent variable; and (v) a front-loaded ethical framework, including the shutdown-right dilemma for agents that have formed a continuous self. The paper is a theoretical and engineering research preprint. No empirical results are claimed; all described experiments are prospective. Target communities include researchers in developmental artificial intelligence, embodied cognition, artificial consciousness, developmental robotics, and philosophy of mind.

papers.title: Half Cauchy-Modified Exponential Uncertainty Quantification for Tethered Satellites Using the Kalmag Geomagnetic Field Model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we seek the impact of non‑Gaussian heavy-tailed uncertainty in the dynamics of an inextensible tethered satellite due to Earth’s oblateness (J2) and geomagnetic influences. The residual geomagnetic field error is modeled using the Half Cauchy‑modified Exponential (HCME) distribution. It correlates positive heavy‑tailed noise. Realistic mean magnetic fields and their uncertainties are given by the high-resolution Kalmag model. Using Monte Carlo framework, we propagate the stochastic torque through the nonlinear equations of motion taking 10,000 realizations. We derive the stochastic differential equation governing the tether angle, providing complete mathematical characterization of the HCME noise and perform rigorous statistical inferences- maximum likelihood estimation of noise parameters, bootstrap confidence intervals for excedance probabilities and Kolmogorov‑Smirnov test comparing output distributions. Results show that the HCME model leads to a significant higher probability of extreme tether tension events as compared to Gaussian model with the same variance. Specifically, the probability of exceeding 5 N increases from 1.2% (Gaussian) to 8.3% (HCME), a nearly seven‑fold rise. We provide R code for generating HCME random variates through the Lambert W function and for visualizing the heavy‑tailed noise distribution. The methodology is compatible with Kalmag geomagnetic field model and provides a pathway for data‑driven uncertainty quantification in space tether mission.

papers.title: Pedagogical affordances for professional communication development: a mixed-methods comparison of active learning approaches
papers.abstract: Professional communication is an important learning outcome in higher education, yet different active learning pedagogies may provide different communicative affordances for its development and enactment. This study comparatively examined how four active learning pedagogies-group discussion, role play, case study analysis, and student-led seminars-were associated with professional communication across five dimensions: clarity and precision, logical structuring, adaptability and tone, active listening, and persuasive expression. Using a mixed-methods, within-subject repeated-measures design, data were collected from 72 postgraduate management students across two cohorts. All participants experienced the four pedagogies through a Latin Square rotation. Data were drawn from pre-post self-reports, instructor-rated session-level communication performance, and qualitative reflections. Findings were examined across three analytical levels. At the aggregate level, pre-post results indicated significant gains in students’ self-perceived communication competence across both cohorts. These findings indicate perceived development rather than objective gains in demonstrated competence. At the session level, observed communication performance varied across pedagogical conditions, with group discussion and role play associated with higher performance scores than case study analysis and student-led seminars. At the dimension level, qualitative findings revealed distinct pedagogy-dimension linkages. Group discussion was associated with clarity, logical structuring, active listening, and persuasive expression, whereas role play was particularly associated with adaptability and contextual responsiveness. The findings suggest that active learning pedagogies should not be treated as interchangeable approaches to communication development. Instead, their communicative affordances may be considered in relation to specific instructional objectives and desired dimensions of professional communication. The study contributes a differentiated account of how pedagogical structures shape opportunities for communication enactment and provides an evidence-informed basis for aligning active learning design with professional communication objectives in higher education.

papers.title: Analytical Thinking Opportunities and Students’ Experiences through Active Learning: A Qualitative Case Study in a Middle School EFL Classroom
papers.abstract: This qualitative single-case study examined, based on students’ accounts, how active learning activities integrated into the eighth-grade English as a Foreign Language (EFL) curriculum provided opportunities for analytical thinking and how students experienced these activities. The study was conducted in a public middle school in Türkiye over a six-week period. Curriculum-aligned activities included simulated telephone conversations, dialogue construction, prediction tasks, and collaborative discussions, guided by four active learning dimensions: collaborative learning, active engagement, reflective discussion, and student-centered expression. Data were collected through reflective journals from 25 students and semi-structured interviews with 12 volunteers. Thematic analysis combined a deductive approach to analytical thinking processes with an inductive approach to students’ experiences. Findings indicated opportunities for strategic thinking and problem-solving through adapting explanations, inference-making through contextual and visual clues, and comparison through evaluating alternative expressions and dialogues. Students reported benefits from contextual support, peer interaction, and simulated activities, alongside difficulties interpreting unfamiliar language, uncertainty about their responses, limited individual thinking time, and constraints on self-expression. By examining analytical thinking opportunities alongside students’ cognitive and affective experiences, the study illustrates how existing EFL curriculum activities can provide opportunities for analytical engagement while highlighting the importance of instructional support and conditions for participation. This offers a context-sensitive understanding of both the opportunities and limitations of integrating analytical thinking opportunities into regular EFL curriculum.

papers.title: A Machine Learning-Enhanced Ligand-Based Workflow Identifies Novel Cryptosporidium parvum Inhibitors
papers.abstract: Abstract Cryptosporidium parasites are a leading cause of waterborne disease worldwide, causing life-threatening diarrhea and malnutrition in young children and people with HIV. Currently, nitazoxanide is the only FDA-approved treatment, but it is largely ineffective in severely immunocompromised patients, highlighting the need for new therapies. Here, we use a ligand-based virtual screening workflow that integrates Thompson Sampling, a pharmacophore model, and a machine learning classifier to screen a subset of Enamine’s REAL database comprising 51 million virtual compounds. Across two screening campaigns, 20 novel micromolar hits were identified among 69 tested compounds (29%), eight of which exhibited confirmed activity at or below 21 μM. These findings expand the chemical diversity of the original series by introducing new tail and head chemotypes and demonstrate the effectiveness of active learning strategies for improving ligand-based virtual screening performance.

papers.title: Mechanical and ultrasonic characterization of polyamide 11-copper composites manufactured with diverse scanning strategies and energy density parameters
papers.abstract: Abstract Selective laser sintering is a laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing method enabling the fabrication of polymers and composites. This study aims to investigate the influence of scanning strategy and energy density on the mechanical behavior and microstructural characteristics of PA11 and dendritic copper-reinforced PA11 structures. Three distinct hatching strategies were employed, with the energy density systematically varied. A comprehensive characterization was conducted, including radiographic inspection, tensile testing, ultrasonic measurements and scanning electron microscopy analysis. The elastic modulus was determined for different orthogonal faces of cubic specimens using time-of-flight data obtained via ultrasonic measurements, and the anisotropy in their elastic properties was subsequently evaluated. Results demonstrate that tensile strength is significantly affected by the scanning strategy, with the 45/135 alternating hatching strategy yielding lower tensile strength than other strategies. In contrast, increasing energy density promotes sintering, leading to a denser microstructure, improved interparticle bonding, and, consequently, higher elastic modulus values. Furthermore, Ultrasonic evaluation demonstrates anisotropic elastic behavior that depends on both the scanning strategy and the energy density. The study contributes to a better understanding of the relationship between additive manufacturing parameters and mechanical behavior, as well as the potential application of ultrasonic measurement in material characterization.

papers.title: Development of problem-posing instructional materials in teaching mathematics in grade 8
papers.abstract: This study explores the development and implementation of problem-posing instructional materials (PPIM) aimed at enhancing mathematical creativity, problem-solving skills, and attitudes toward mathematics among Grade 8 students. Employing a descriptive-developmental research design, the study followed the ADDIE model—Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation—and integrated the Active Learning Framework (ALF) to create instructional content. A total of 139 grade 8 students participated. The instructional materials were assessed using Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovation framework, achieving a high acceptability rating of 5.78 (96.3%). The study demonstrated significant improvements in student attitudes toward mathematics, evidenced by a post-survey p-value of 0.0008. Students progressed in problem-solving (summative score: 80.4%) and creativity fluency (85.1%). However, problem construction, confidence, and comprehension challenges were identified through focus group discussions. The study highlights the value of structured, visually engaging materials in boosting mathematics engagement and skills, noting the need to improve resources and instructional clarity.

papers.title: Machine Learning for Stress Detection: A LightGBM-Based Approach Using Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Stress is an important physiological and psychological reaction which, when prolonged, has a negative impact on the health and well-being of humans. Traditional stress assessment methods tend to be subjective and are not scalable in real-time. In this research, a lightweight machine learning framework to predict stress from easily measurable environmental and activity-related features, temperature, humidity, and steps, is introduced. The proposed method is different from the approach that depends on complex physiological signals and uses minimal non-invasive inputs that can be applied in the wearable and IoT field. The stress level is considered as the target variable, and all the features used as input variables are independent from each other to prevent data leakage. There are several machine learning and deep learning models and their performances are measured, such as LightGBM, Support vector machine (SVM), AdaBoost, Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU). Bayesian hyperparameter optimization is used to improve the performance of the model and guarantee strong generalization. Experimental results show that LightGBM outperforms the other models, giving an accuracy of 97% and a balanced precision, recall and F1 score of 95%. The results demonstrate promising predictive performance on the evaluated dataset. However, since the model was validated on a relatively small publicly available dataset, further evaluation using larger and more diverse real-world datasets is required before practical deployment.

papers.title: A Generative AI-Integrated Framework for Teaching Operations Management: Case-Based Projects
papers.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GAI) reshapes business education, instructors must simultaneously safeguard academic integrity and develop students’ AI literacy for an increasingly AI-driven workplace. This study developed the GAI Learning Framework (GLF), a replicable, step-by-step experiential learning approach for case-based projects in undergraduate business courses, illustrated through an operations management (OM) application. Rather than enabling passive cognitive offloading, the GLF promotes active learning by requiring students to craft context-rich prompts grounded in course materials, systematically compare outputs across multiple GAI platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini), and critically evaluate discrepancies against independently verified sources. The framework was implemented across two sections of an undergraduate OM course and evaluated using a student survey that combined Likert-scale items with open-ended reflections (n = 50). All three constructs exceeded the scale midpoint, with pooled means ranging from 3.93 (Constructive Alignment) to 4.08 (Cognitive Load/Scaffolding). Qualitative student reflections further indicated that students perceived the framework as fostering active learning, AI platform literacy, and professional communication skills. This study offers educators a practical, classroom-tested framework for integrating GAI tools into case-based projects in business courses while preserving analytical rigor and promoting experiential learning. Supplemental Material: The online appendices are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/ited.2026.0224 .
