papers.title: Short-Term Power Load Forecasting Based on Interpretable Time-Frequency Dual-Domain Fusion
papers.abstract: Real-world power load series exhibit pronounced non-stationarity and complex spatiotemporal dependencies, while the black-box nature of deep learning limits its credibility in industrial dispatching. This paper proposes a probabilistic short-term load forecasting model integrating multi-scale temporal modeling and learnable frequency-domain filtering to improve forecasting accuracy, uncertainty quantification, and interpretability. The model employs parallel temporal and frequency branches. The temporal branch uses multi-scale patches to capture local fluctuations and long-range dependencies, while the frequency branch applies a learnable complex-valued filter to extract dominant global seasonal periodicities. A dynamic gating mechanism adaptively fuses features from both domains, and quantile regression generates prediction intervals. On the Quanzhou and Australian datasets, the proposed model achieves mean absolute percentage errors of 0.49% and 0.77%, respectively. The corresponding prediction interval coverage probabilities are 79.18% and 80.65%, both close to the nominal coverage of 80%. A SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based post hoc attribution framework further identifies key factors influencing predictions through feature contributions. The results suggest that the proposed model effectively combines local temporal fluctuations with global frequency-domain periodic information and provides a degree of post hoc interpretability, supporting accurate probabilistic load forecasting and a clearer understanding of the model’s predictions.

papers.title: Tunable microscale assembly with ultrasound vortex tweezers
papers.abstract: Abstract Ultrasound tweezers provide a powerful approach for the contactless manipulation of microscale objects, yet achieving structurally simple platforms capable of tunable particle assembly remains challenging. Here we introduce ultrasound vortex tweezers based on a Fresnel-spiral diffraction grating (FSDG) that converts an incident ultrasonic plane wave into a vortex beam carrying orbital angular momentum. The passive grating structure enables the generation of ultrasound vortex fields with tunable topological charge, producing ring-shaped trapping regions with adjustable spatial scales. Operating at 10 MHz, the system provides improved spatial confinement compared with conventional low-frequency ultrasound tweezers. Using this platform, we demonstrate controllable self-rotation of individual microparticles, tunable aggregation of multiple particles, and core-shell encapsulation in bidisperse particle systems. The rotational speed of trapped particles shows an overall increasing trend with increasing vortex order, while the aggregation and encapsulation processes can be regulated through vortex order, driving voltage, and actuation time. These results establish ultrasound vortex tweezers as a compact and versatile strategy for tunable microscale assembly, offering new opportunities for high-precision ultrasound manipulation in materials engineering and biofabrication.

papers.title: Finite-time ESO-based model predictive control for hierarchical robust tracking of UAVs
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the problem of accurate and fast trajectory and attitude tracking for a quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) against unknown external disturbances. To address this issue, a finite-time extended state observer-based model predictive control framework is proposed to enable hierarchical robust tracking performance. Specifically, a finite-time extended state observer (FTESO) with a simplified finite-time convergence term is developed to estimate the lumped disturbances, reducing the structural complexity of the observer while retaining fast finite-time convergence. Next, the real-time disturbance estimates are incorporated into the prediction model to compensate for the mismatch between the nominal model and the actual quadrotor dynamics. On this basis, a Lyapunov-based model predictive control (MPC) scheme with a contraction constraint is constructed to guarantee the closed-loop stability of the position subsystem. Furthermore, a nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode control (NFTSMC) strategy is designed for the attitude subsystem to achieve finite-time convergence and improved tracking accuracy. Theoretical analysis establishes the stability of the overall closed-loop system. Finally, numerical simulations are conducted under representative disturbance scenarios. By incorporating FTESO, the proposed framework achieves a 14.43% reduction in the position-tracking root mean square error (RMSE), demonstrating the effectiveness of online disturbance compensation in improving tracking performance.

papers.title: Third permanent molar agenesis in children with and without molar incisor hypomineralisation: an international investigation
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose To investigate whether children with molar incisor hypomineralisation (MIH) are more likely to have missing third permanent molars (TPMs) than unaffected peers. Additional objectives were to explore variation in TPM agenesis by sex, geographic region and hypodontia of other permanent teeth. Methods The study was conducted in specialist paediatric dentistry centres across 14 countries. Participants were children with or without MIH, aged between 10 and 17 years. Following informed consent, a validated MIH index was used to assess the presence/extent of any hypomineralised teeth and panoramic radiographs were viewed to record the number and location of any developing TPMs. Results A total of 634 participants were recruited: 264 (41.6%) with MIH and 370 (58.4%) without this condition. Two hundred fifty-five (40.2%) of the overall study population had at least one missing TPM. Logistic regression analysis indicated that neither MIH status nor sex were associated with TPM agenesis. However, TPM agenesis was significantly more likely in participants with hypodontia of other permanent teeth (OR = 2.57, 95% CI 1.42, 4.66, p = 0.002). Geographical region was also statistically significantly associated with TPM agenesis with the lowest prevalence found in the African region (6.3%) and the highest found in the European region (55.9%). Conclusion Within the limitations of this study, children with MIH appear at no greater risk of TPM agenesis than their non-MIH peers; however, clinicians should be aware of marked differences between different geographical regions and the greater likelihood of TPM agenesis in children with hypodontia of other permanent teeth.

papers.title: A tripla articulação na saúde renal – o Chatbot como modelo propositivo de educação (ODS 4) e sustentabilidade (ODS 17) para o bem-estar (ODS 3) dos pacientes dialíticos
papers.abstract: Advances in dialysis treatments have significantly increased the survival of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD); however, health-related quality of life remains compromised, mainly due to functional limitations, strict dietary regimens, and dependence on specialized information. In this context, this study proposes the implementation of an educational Chatbot as a support tool for health literacy, articulating the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of the 2030 Agenda, specifically SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), SDG 4 (Quality Education), and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals). This is a bibliographic, theoretical, and propositional study with a qualitative approach, grounded in classical methodological references (Gil, 2008; Minayo, 2001; Flick, 2009). The Chatbot was designed to function as an informational support instrument, providing content on nutrition, machine alarm management, infection prevention, and catheter care through tablets and the WhatsApp application, both during and outside dialysis sessions. Theoretical results indicate that integrating the Chatbot promotes patient empowerment by transforming treatment time into a period of active learning, while optimizing human and technological resources (SDG 17).

papers.title: Role of Oxides in the Tensile Properties of Pure Copper Processed by Laser Powder Bed Fusion
papers.abstract: Oxide particles can affect the tensile properties of pure Cu processed by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) through their interactions with dislocations. This study compared the microstructure and tensile behavior of samples produced from virgin and oxidized pure Cu powders under identical LPBF conditions. The two samples had comparable relative densities above 98.7% and similar grain sizes. Yield and ultimate tensile strengths were nevertheless higher in the oxidized sample, whereas uniform and total elongations were lower. Backscattered-electron imaging and image analysis indicated that oxide particles occupied a higher apparent area fraction in the examined fields of the oxidized sample; electron backscatter diffraction analysis also showed higher kernel average misorientation. Together, these observations suggest two possible roles for oxide particles: acting as dispersed obstacles to dislocation motion and promoting dislocation retention during LPBF, consistent with the higher kernel average misorientation. The strength increase may therefore reflect both particle strengthening and a greater contribution from dislocation strengthening.

papers.title: Impact of medical law education based on the IRAC model on the medical law reasoning of internal medicine and surgery residents
papers.abstract: Medical-legal challenges have intensified over the past decade, leading to substantial financial burdens and psychological distress for physicians. Literature reviews indicate that the medical law skills of specialists and residents, particularly their medical law reasoning abilities, are insufficient, underscoring the necessity for appropriate educational interventions. This study aimed to determine the impact of medical law education based on the IRAC (Issue, Rule, Analysis, Conclusion) model on the medical law reasoning of internal medicine and surgery residents at Zanjan University of Medical Sciences. A quasi-experimental study employing a non-randomized control group with a pretest-posttest design was conducted. The ADDIE model guided the design of the educational intervention. Residents were non-randomly assigned to an intervention group ( n = 27) receiving IRAC-based training and a control group ( n = 27) receiving no such training. Attitudes toward medical law reasoning were assessed using the Medical Law Reasoning Attitude Questionnaire (MLRAQ), while cognitive medical law reasoning was assessed using the participant-completed, scenario-based Medical Law Reasoning Skill Test (MLRST), which measures respondents’ reasoning judgments in hypothetical medico-legal scenarios. Data were analyzed using independent t-test, paired t-test, Chi-square, and Welch. No statistically significant differences were observed between the groups in baseline total attitude scores ( P = 0.213) or total medical law reasoning skill scores ( P = 0.572). Posttest results, however, revealed significant differences favoring the intervention group in total attitude scores (101.48 ± 9.32 vs. 82.63 ± 13.08; P < 0.001) and all its subscales. Similarly, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher total medical law reasoning skill scores posttest (79.00 ± 8.27 vs. 58.81 ± 7.39; P < 0.001) across all subscales. The primary between-group analysis of pretest-to-posttest change confirmed these improvements for both outcomes ( P < 0.001), and supplementary Welch’s tests on posttest scores were consistent. The IRAC-based medical law education intervention was associated with significant improvements in residents’ measured attitudes and cognitive reasoning scores. This model offers a practical framework for medical educators and curriculum planners to employ creative, integrated, model-based, and active learning strategies to enhance legal reasoning competencies. Ultimately, fostering these skills may help reduce future legal disputes, mitigate physicians’ criminal and civil liabilities, and ensure better adherence to patient rights.

papers.title: PENGEMBANGAN LEMBAR KERJA PESERTA DIDIK (LKPD) DIGITAL BERBASIS PROBLEM BASED LEARNING (PBL) DALAM PEMBELAJARAN MATEMATIKA SISWA
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop a digital student worksheet (LKPD) based on Problem Based Learning (PBL) that is valid, practical, and effective for junior high school mathematics learning. Initial observations in Grade VIII at SMPS St. Antonius Padua Leworahang indicated that students tended to be passive and had difficulty understanding mathematical concepts. The digital PBL-based worksheet was designed to combine problem-based active learning with interactive digital media. This research and development study used the Plomp model, comprising preliminary investigation, design, realization/construction, test, evaluation and revision, and implementation. The participants were Grade VIII students at SMPS St. Antonius Padua Leworahang. Data were collected using material, media, and practitioner validation forms, a readability questionnaire, a student response questionnaire, and a mathematical conceptual understanding test. Validation scores were 96.77% for material experts, 94.12% for media experts, and 100% for practitioners; all were classified as very valid. The readability score was 96%, while student responses reached 97%, classified as very practical. In the large-scale trial, the learning completion rate reached 85%, classified as very effective. These findings indicate that the developed digital PBL-based worksheet is suitable for supporting mathematics learning.

papers.title: Hybrid Epidemiological–Neural Modelling of Dengue Under Climate-Socioeconomic Influence
papers.abstract: Dengue transmission in climate-sensitive and socioeconomically heterogeneous settings arises from nonlinear interactions between environmental suitability, mosquito ecology, and human behaviour. Classical SEIR-type models offer mechanistic interpretability but are often constrained by observational noise and incomplete data, while purely data-driven approaches typically fail to respect underlying transmission dynamics. In this study, we introduce a hybrid epidemiological framework that embeds a temperature–unemployment driven SEIR–SEI model within a Physics-Informed Neural Network (SEIR–PINN). Using weekly dengue incidence data from Medellín, Colombia, we incorporate unemployment as a socioeconomic proxy that modulates transmission alongside climatic suitability. The Model performance was evaluated in two ways; the prediction of observed incidence, the SEIR–PINN achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 15.05 and R2 of 0.975, compared with MAE of 43.57 and R2 of 0.870 for a mechanistic SEIR–SEI baseline fitted under identical climatic and socioeconomic assumptions. Shuffled five-fold cross-validation provided held-out prediction of observed incidence within the 2009–2011 period, with mean MAE of 14.87 and mean R2 of 0.977 (out-of-fold MAE 14.89, R2 0.978). These held-out results interpolate within the observed epidemic and are not an assessment of prospective forecasting performance Importantly, the SEIR–PINN reconstructs latent human and mosquito compartments that remain biologically consistent across epidemic phases. By fusing mechanistic structure with data-adaptive flexibility, the proposed SEIR–PINN provides an interpretable framework for analysing the joint climatic and socioeconomic modulation of dengue transmission in an urban endemic setting. Although using Medellín as a single-city methodological case study, application of this framework to other dengue endemic settings requires external validation using additional locations, longer time periods, and independent datasets. The results therefore support the potential use of physics-informed hybrid models as interpretable tools for dengue surveillance and transmission-dynamics research, while recognising the need for further external validation across longer time periods and additional geographical regions.

papers.title: Thermal Analysis of an Exponential Longitudinally Porous Fin with Hybrid Nanoliquid Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Fins are widely used in industry, especially in heat exchangers, because they are small, light, and inexpensive. Artificial neural networks (ANNs) have become an important tool for modelling complex, nonlinear heat and flow behaviour, especially where conventional numerical methods are too costly or impractical. This study uses an artificial intelligence (AI)-based numerical approach to analyse steady-state heat transfer in an exponentially profiled longitudinal porous fin wetted with a hybrid nanoliquid. The governing ordinary differential equation (ODE) is formulated using Darcy's law and Fourier's law of heat conduction, and it is reduced to dimensionless form using suitable dimensionless variables and boundary conditions. The physics-informed neural network (PINN) solution is validated against the bvp5c solver, and the two are in close agreement. The results show that the hybrid nanoliquid and the temperature-dependent properties of the exponential fin have a significant effect on the temperature distribution. Furthermore, the PINN and bvp5c results agree well with earlier published studies.

papers.title: Revisão de literatura inovações tecnológicas com mãos biônicas controladas por sinais elétricos cerebrais no ensino de Física
papers.abstract: Investigative practical classes are an important and fundamental tool in physics education, as they enable students to become protagonists of their own learning by drawing on prior knowledge, putting into practice what has been learned in theoretical classes, and constructing new knowledge. Physics education in basic education faces challenges related to classroom instruction, abstract content, the lack of contextualization in pedagogical practices, and students’ difficulties in understanding concepts. An important stimulus for enriching demonstrations involves the use of teaching resources aligned with active learning methodologies. In this context, biotechnology emerges as a promising pedagogical tool, particularly when associated with devices that concretely illustrate physical concepts. Among these resources, attention-controlled (concentration-based) bionic hand models stand out, as they enable the simultaneous exploration of physics content within an investigative and practical perspective. The present study aims to analyze, through a non-systematic literature review, the didactic potential of biotechnology in physics education, with an emphasis on basic education. The methodology was based on an exploratory search of scientific articles, books, theses, dissertations, and educational documents, without a defined time frame, prioritizing studies addressing the integration of technology, science, and interdisciplinary practices in the school context. The results indicate that incorporating biotechnological resources, such as bionic hands, promotes active learning, stimulates scientific curiosity, and enhances the understanding of abstract concepts through experimentation and contextualized problem-solving. Furthermore, these practices contribute to the development of cognitive, technical, and socio-emotional skills, promoting a more inclusive and meaningful educational approach in accordance with current guidelines for science and technology education. It is concluded that incorporating biotechnology as a teaching resource in physics education represents an innovative and effective pedagogical strategy, with the potential to transform the classroom into a dynamic, investigative, and interdisciplinary learning environment.

papers.title: Through‐Build Wear Investigation of Vertically Oriented LPBF AlSi10Mg Specimens
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT AlSi10Mg components with refined microstructures can be created with laser powder bed fusion (LPBF); however, tribological performance may exhibit build‐height‐dependent variations possibly resulting from thermal gradients during the building process. The layer‐wise tribological response of vertically fabricated LPBF AlSi10Mg components under dry sliding conditions is examined in this work. It was assessed under controlled conditions using LPBF samples produced at a laser power of 400 W, 1200 mm/s scan speed , 0.12 mm hatch spacing , and 40 µm layer thickness . Pin‐on‐disc wear experiments were conducted using samples across various build zones with a load of 40 N for 750 s, and the track diameter was 50 mm, with a total sliding distance of 1500 mm. To determine variances in performance throughout the build direction, rates of wear and frictional behavior have been examined for each layer. The LPBF process may cause changes in microstructure and defect distribution along the build direction, potentially influenced by variations in thermal history. These microstructural variations result in the lowest wear in subsurface layers and the highest wear in central layers. These findings demonstrate the necessity of considering layer‐wise position, which has been unexplored in previous tribological research studies and is useful in critical defense and aerospace applications.

papers.title: Machine learning-based prediction of microstructural evolution during heat treatment of high-entropy alloys: A comprehensive review
papers.abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are multi-principal-element material systems in which five or more elements are combined in approximately equimolar proportions. They have attracted sustained scientific attention because they can unite mechanical, thermal, and chemical properties that surpass those of conventional single-principal-element alloys. Heat treatment is a principal lever for tuning HEA microstructures: annealing, homogenisation, ageing, and solution treatment each alter phase fractions, precipitate morphologies, grain size distributions, and dislocation substructures in ways that ultimately determine suitability for demanding aerospace, energy-generation, or biomedical service conditions. The experimental exploration of this enormous compositional and processing space is, however, prohibitively expensive and time-consuming when pursued through conventional trial-and-error metallurgy alone. The emerging closed-loop paradigm, in which ML models predict microstructural outcomes, active learning selects the next experiment, and automated characterisation closes the feedback loop, represents the critical frontier of HEA heat-treatment science, enabling systematic navigation of composition-processing-microstructure space at throughputs unachievable by purely experimental campaigns. Machine learning (ML) methods including random forests, gradient-boosted trees, artificial neural networks, support vector machines, Gaussian process regressors, graph neural networks, convolutional neural networks, long short-term memory networks, and physics-informed deep learning architectures, offer a fundamentally different paradigm: they extract quantitative structure-property-processing relationships directly from accumulated datasets, then generalise those relationships to compositions and heat treatment schedules that have never been physically tested. This review synthesises the state of the art in ML-assisted prediction of microstructural evolution during the heat treatment of HEAs. We trace the foundational metallurgical concepts governing HEA phase selection and microstructural development, survey the construction and curation of datasets on which ML models are trained, evaluate principal algorithms and their relative merits and shortcomings, and discuss the integration of ML with CALPHAD thermodynamic frameworks and physics-informed constraints. We then identify critical open challenges such as data scarcity, transferability, interpretability, and the treatment of kinetic pathways and propose research directions expected to define the next decade of work in this field. The scope of this review is deliberately bounded: it covers ML methods applied to heat-treatment-induced microstructural evolution, including phase fraction, precipitate morphology, grain size, and sigma-phase formation in HEAs and directly related MPEA systems; coverage of room-temperature mechanical property prediction, corrosion, and coating deposition is included only where it directly informs microstructural evolution modelling. Although Section 10 gives particular attention to surface engineering and high-entropy coating applications, the methods reviewed are equally applicable to bulk structural alloys for aerospace and nuclear service, biomedical implant alloys, hydrogen-storage hydrides, thermoelectric devices, and energy-storage electrodes; this breadth is addressed in Section 10.4. The review encompasses 106 verifiable primary references distributed across 12 sections and 15 original figures.

papers.title: Defining Osseointegration for Biodegradable Scaffolds based on Histological, Immunohistochemical and Ultrastructural Analysis.
papers.abstract: Osseointegration of metal implants refers to the formation of a direct, intimate, and stable interface between bone and the implant surface under physiological loads, without intervening fibrous tissue. This concept is largely based on the long-term fixation of non-degradable implants, where bone remodeling occurs around a permanent material. However, there is no equivalent framework defining de biological integration of biodegradable scaffolds used for scaffold-guided bone regeneration (SGBR), whose architecture, mechanical properties, and surface chemistry are intentionally desined to change over time. Consequently, definitions developed for permanent mettalic are frequently applied to biodegradable scaffolds, leading to uncertainty regarding whether these scaffolds truly "osseointegrate". We argue that the biological processes at biodegradable scaffold-bone interfaces fundamentally differs from that of metallic implants, and should be distinguished. Rather than classical "bone anchorage", biodegradable scaffolds support a dynamic, immunologically active, and mechanically evolving bone-scaffold interface in which fibrous encapsulation and bone formation compete. This paper aims to clarify these issues not by redefining osseointegration in general, but by adapting it specifically to osteoconductive biodegradable scaffolds in SGBR. Using evidence from a series of studies in well-characterised large-animal models of segmental bone defects, we propose a new framework that captures the temporal, cellular, and structural complexities of osseointegration of biodegradable scaffolds in living organisms. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Biodegradable scaffolds are intended to facilitate bone regeneration and gradually degrade as new tissue develops. Nevertheless, there is limited knowledge about how these materials interact with bone over extended periods. This research examines the bone-scaffold interface over 36-months using histology, immunohistochemistry, scanning electron microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy. Results indicate that biodegradable scaffolds do not form the permanent bonds commonly defined as osseointegration in metallic implants. Instead, they establish a dynamic interface that evolves as the organ bone, composed of mineralised tissue, blood vessels, and extracellular matrix, remodels around the degrading scaffold. These insights improve our understanding of scaffold-guided bone regeneration and will guide the development of next-generation biodegradable scaffolds that shorten the timeframe and better support long-term bone growth.

papers.title: Finite Element Method for Sustainable Structural Integrity of Multi-bolted Flanges: A Review of Optimized Design and Green Maintenance Strategies
papers.abstract: Multi-bolted flange (MBF) connections are essential components of piping systems, pressure vessels, offshore structures, renewable energy infrastructure, and process plants. However, their long-term reliability is often affected by complex mechanical loading, thermal cycling, gasket degradation, corrosion, bolt preload loss, and uneven force distributions. These technical challenges can lead to leakage, fatigue failure, unplanned shutdowns, repeated component replacement, and increased material waste. This review examines the role of the Finite Element Method (FEM) in improving the sustainable structural integrity of MBF systems through optimised design and green maintenance strategies. Recent studies have been synthesised to show how FEM supports stress distribution analysis, bolt preload evaluation, gasket contact-pressure prediction, fatigue life assessment, leakage prevention, corrosion risk evaluation, and structural health monitoring. Particular attention is given to how FEM-driven modelling can reduce overdesign, improve sealing performance, extend service life, and support predictive maintenance by identifying critical failure mechanisms before field failure. This review also highlights the importance of bolt modelling conditions, including preload definition, contact interaction, gasket compressibility, frictional behaviour, mesh refinement, and service-induced load combinations. Although FEM has significantly advanced the understanding of MBF performance, important research gaps remain in the integration of FEM with self-healing materials, real-time adaptive control, sensor-based monitoring, machine learning validation, and digital twin maintenance frameworks. Overall, this review demonstrates that FEM provides a practical pathway for achieving safer, more reliable, and more resource-efficient MBF systems while supporting sustainable engineering and environmental protection.

papers.title: End-to-end differentiable gust and maneuver loads at large scale via concurrent simulations
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a new method for large-scale computation of aerodynamic loads for aircraft and airframe sizing. It is built on a geometrically nonlinear aeroelastic simulation framework with concurrent capabilities that can be deployed on modern hardware architectures. It enables the construction of load envelopes for static and dynamic cases in computational times of the order of seconds, as well as uncertainty quantification analysis via massively-parallel Monte Carlo simulations, while offering seamless integration with industrial-scale aircraft models. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis of the dynamic loads on concurrent computations is achieved via the use of state-of-the-art strategies for automatic differentiation and the extensive use of collective communication primitives. We demonstrate its use on a high-aspect-ratio-wing aircraft configuration, showing the ability of the solvers to capture nonlinear effects for external forces inducing large deformations and also the importance of these effects when studying modern aircraft concepts. Discrete, maneuver and gust loads are assessed for multiple flow and parametric conditions running concurrently. Sensitivities of maximum wing-root stresses and tip displacements are efficiently computed across all those conditions and verified against finite differences.

papers.title: AI-BASED DIGITAL TWIN FOR EV BATTERY HEALTH MONITORING
papers.abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) rely on lithium-ion batteries whose capacity, power capability, and performance change with temperature, charging patterns, operating conditions, and aging. Conventional battery management systems (BMS) monitor voltage, current, and temperature, but important battery states such as state of charge (SOC), state of health (SOH), and remaining useful life (RUL) must be estimated. An artificial-intelligence-enabled digital twin provides a virtual representation of a physical battery by combining real-time measurements, mathematical models, historical data, and predictive algorithms. This review examines digital-twin architecture, battery degradation, model-based estimation, machine-learning techniques, data preparation, and validation strategies for EV battery health monitoring. It discusses the use of extended Kalman filters, gradient-boosting algorithms, and deep-learning methods for estimating battery states and predicting degradation. The review also identifies challenges related to data quality, model generalization, uncertainty, computational requirements, and cybersecurity. A conceptual architecture and implementation workflow are proposed for developing a data-driven battery health monitoring prototype. The study establishes a foundation for future implementation and experimental evaluation using publicly available battery datasets.

papers.title: A Review on AI-Based Process Monitoring and Quality Control for Additive Cladding Technologies in Industrial Component Remanufacturing
papers.abstract: With the transition toward global carbon neutrality and a circular economy, remanufacturing technologies for high-value industrial components have gained significant attention. Additive cladding processes such as laser cladding, directed energy deposition (DED), wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), and plasma transferred arc (PTA) are key solutions for localized structural restoration. However, dynamic melt pool instability and complex thermal histories often induce defects like porosity and microcracks, degrading product reliability. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted multi-sensor monitoring and closed-loop control systems have been introduced to enhance process stability and repeatability. This review comprehensively categorizes additive cladding processes for remanufacturing and explores recent advancements in AI-driven sensing, deep-learning-based defect prediction, adaptive feedback control, and digital twin integration. Finally, critical technical challenges and future perspectives for industrial deployment are discussed.

papers.title: Machine Learning for Composite Biomaterials in Bone Implants and Scaffolds: A Systematic Review of Manufacturing and the Process–Structure–Property–Performance Relationships
papers.abstract: Bone-implant and scaffold research is beginning to use machine learning (ML) alongside biomaterials design and advanced manufacturing, but the literature is scattered across different material classes and stages of development. We therefore reviewed ML studies relevant to composite, multiphase, coated, graded, and multimaterial systems and organized them using the process-structure-property-performance (PSPP) sequence. PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were used as the formal bibliographic databases; IEEE Xplore screening, targeted OpenAlex searches, and Google Scholar citation chasing provided supplementary coverage. The frozen dataset contained 46 primary studies. Twenty-five satisfied a strict composite/multimaterial definition, whereas 21 were retained as boundary-supporting evidence for the sensitivity analysis. The studies show that ML is being used for property prediction, surrogate modeling, inverse design, multi-objective optimization, and material screening. Validation, however, did not advance at the same pace as modeling. Physical or experimental confirmation was identified in 32/46 studies (69.6%), in vitro or in vivo experiments, including antibacterial assays, in 11/46 (23.9%), and external validation in only 2/46 (4.3%); none reported prospective clinical validation. Explicit uncertainty analysis and strong reproducibility were also uncommon. Taken together, the literature suggests that the main challenge is no longer demonstrating that an ML model can fit a biomaterials dataset. The more difficult task is showing that a model-guided choice remains useful after fabrication and biological testing. Priorities therefore include better-described multimodal datasets, independent and leakage-resistant validation, characterization of the manufactured rather than only nominal structure, uncertainty-aware design, physics-informed modeling, and prospective biological testing.

papers.title: Facilitating access to cardiopulmonary resuscitation training in high-risk underserved communities: a realist evidence synthesis
papers.abstract: Members of the public are vital in improving survival from an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) by calling Emergency Medical Services, performing cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and using a defibrillator. However, some parts of England, with higher incidence of OHCA with lower rates of lay rescuer CPR are usually more socioeconomically disadvantaged and ethnically diverse areas. Increasing access to resuscitation skills training may help address this disparity, however little is known about the factors influencing people’s decisions to intervene and how best to engage people from these communities. We aimed to develop initial realist programme theory (IPT) of how, why, in which contexts and with what impacts interventions can engage people from minoritized ethnic groups in CPR training. This theory provides information on contexts in which mechanisms (resources and people’s responses to them) might work to produce outcomes that contribute to facilitating training access. Using ITPs with formal behaviour change theory is an innovative approach. Together they can provide detailed theory to inform intervention development. We conducted a realist evidence synthesis of published literature and primary data collected from four workshops with South Asian and Black African and Caribbean communities in socioeconomically disadvantaged areas of England. The resulting IPT is expressed as eight context-mechanism-outcome (CMO) configurations. The IPT covers chronological stages that must be addressed to facilitate underserved community members’ participation in resuscitation skills training; 1) gaining access to communities and overcoming mistrust of people perceived as outsiders or establishment figures; 2) addressing practical and contextual obstacles to training attendance and 3) creating a training environment that promotes engagement and uses activities informed by behaviour change techniques that encourage deeper and active learning. Building trusting and collaborative relationships with influential trusted voices from communities runs through all chronological stages. Addressing obstacles to training attendance and creating a training environment that includes culturally informed 2-way discussion of concerns, opportunity to rehearse dealing with potential barriers to acting as well as practical skills training all informed by behaviour change techniques could contribute to successful training. We contribute nuanced theoretical understanding taking into account contextual factors, of what might work for whom, how and why to facilitate access to resuscitation skills training for underserved communities to inform future intervention development, implementation and evaluation. Building trust and collaborative working with communities underpin this theory. ISRCTN. Registration date 28/03/2023. https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN90350842 .

papers.title: Predictive analysis of Drug concentration in drug release process via two-dimensional mechanistic model and machine learning integrated Grey Wolf optimization
papers.abstract: This research develops a machine learning framework to predict the spatial distribution of drug concentration (C) within a specific cylindrical biomaterial matrix at a fixed release time (t = 2400 s), using the radial (r) and axial (z) coordinates as inputs. The predictions are limited to the specific diffusion-reaction system described by the mass transfer equations, and the parameter set defined by Maxwell method, with no extrapolation beyond the training domain of r ∈ [0, 0.006] m and z ∈ [0, 0.009] m. Three distinct models, Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), were employed to predict C based on the input parameters r and z. The data for machine learning were obtained by solution of mass transfer equations for this specific system. The effectiveness of each model was evaluated by considering essential metrics, such as the R² score, the Mean Squared Error (MSE), and the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). The findings suggest that the XGBoost model surpassed both GPR and KRR, attaining an R² score of 0.97322, showcasing its effectiveness in capturing the inherent patterns within the dataset. GPR also demonstrated good performance with an R² score of 0.95911, whereas KRR exhibited lower accuracy with an R² score of 0.75277. To enhance the models’ predictive capabilities, hyperparameter optimization was carried out using Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO). Within the specific simulated system investigated, this study demonstrates the efficacy of ML models with hyperparameter optimization for predicting spatial drug concentration. Extension to other systems requires additional validation.

papers.title: When an AI Solves the Physics: How Firm Is Each Answer? A Neural Operator Read at Several of Its Own Resolutions
papers.abstract: Neural operators are AI models that learn the laws of a physical system, such as the flow of air, water or plasma. They answer questions about it far faster than classical solvers, and they are used for weather, fusion, chip design and medical devices. Each answer comes with no sign of how firm it is. This concept note reviews the main published work on neural operators and marks where an answer can go wrong without any sign. It covers the Fourier Neural Operator, the neural operator library, the Nature Machine Intelligence paper on extending architectures to function spaces, conformal prediction for operator learning, the discretization-error analysis of Fourier neural operators, and the ICLR 2026 study of zero-shot super-resolution. The note then describes a simple check for each case. A neural operator is built to run at any grid, so the grid is one of its own permitted settings. The computer makes 2 to 4 versions of the same run by moving only the model's own permitted settings: the normal setting and settings near both ends of the permitted range. The same trained model reads every version, unchanged. The spread between the versions is inversely proportional to the leading eigenvalue, so a wide spread means the answer is near a tipping point, such as a plasma disruption or the change from smooth to turbulent flow. A computer-decided shunting action then sends only the doubtful cases to a classical solver, and all other cases carry on. It needs no retraining and no new data. Patent pending. Keywords: neural operators, Fourier neural operator, scientific machine learning, resolution, discretization, tipping point, spread value, shunting action

papers.title: การพฒนาทกษะการอานออกเสยง สระเสยงสน ภาษาองกฤษ โดยใชเทคนคโฟนกส ของนกเรยนชนประถมศกษาปท 1 โรงเรยนสาธตละอออทศ กรงเทพมหานคร: DEVELOPMENT OF ENGLISH SHORT VOWELS PRONUNCIATION SKILL WITH PHONICS TECHNIQUE OF GRADE 1 STUDENTS AT LA-ORUTIS DEMONSTRATION SCHOOL, BANGKOK

This research employed a quasi-experimental research design. The population consisted of 78 Grade 1 students at La-orutis Demonstration School, Bangkok, in the 2025 academic year. The sample used in this study consisted of Grade 1 students in the second semester of the 2025 academic year, including 25 students from Grade 1/3 as the experimental group receiving instruction through the phonics technique and 25 students from Grade 1/1 as the control group receiving conventional instruction. The research instruments consisted of phonics-based lesson plans, conventional lesson plans, an English short vowel pronunciation skill test, and a student satisfaction questionnaire. The statistics used for data analysis were mean, standard deviation, and t-test. The findings revealed that: (1) the students who learned through the phonics technique demonstrated significantly higher English short vowel pronunciation skill after learning than before learning at the .01 level of statistical significance. After the instruction, the students were able to blend consonant and short vowel sounds more accurately, read short words independently, reduce guessing and word memorization behaviors, and gain greater confidence in pronunciation. (2) the students who learned through the phonics technique demonstrated significantly higher English short vowel pronunciation skill than those who learned through conventional instruction at the .01 level of statistical significance. This was because the phonics technique helped students understand the relationship between letters and sounds, enabling them to segment, blend, and read unfamiliar words more effectively, whereas conventional instruction mainly emphasized repetition and word memorization. (3) Grade 1 students showed satisfaction toward learning through the phonics technique at a high level. The students demonstrated greater interest and participation in classroom activities, showed more confidence in speaking English in front of the class, and exhibited more active learning behaviors.

papers.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
papers.abstract: Planning with world models enables test-time adaptation for embodied agents, offering superior generalization over direct policy learning. However, long-horizon tasks remain hindered by cumulative errors and search complexity. Existing hierarchical methods often use rigid macro-actions or latent skills, leading to brittle representations and limited fine-grained control. We introduce ID-WM (Implicit Dynamics World Models), a hierarchical world model that decouples state-space reachability from local control. Our framework utilizes a high-level model to sample feasible transitions across the state manifold and a low-level world model as an inverse dynamics solver to ground these transitions into precise actions. This allows the planner to identify reachable subgoals without being constrained by low-level execution details. By prioritizing local physical feasibility over global behavioral patterns, ID-WM synthesizes novel long-horizon plans from short segments, transcending the specific behavioral modes seen during training. We demonstrate its effectiveness across three navigation and manipulation suites, achieving a 38.5% improvement over state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners. Crucially, by leveraging this hierarchical structure to mitigate compounding errors, our approach yields a 135% performance gain over single-level world model MPC, particularly in complex, unseen configurations for long-horizon tasks. Videos can be viewed at https://id-wm.github.io

papers.title: Hard Constraint Projection in a Physics Informed Neural Network (Burgers)
papers.abstract: Physics informed machine learning provides a framework to study and simulate fluid dynamics, potentially at a fraction of the computational cost of traditional numerical methods, with the goal of improving the explainability, accuracy and robustness of purely data driven machine learning methods. In this work, we extend the hard constraint projection (HCP) method developed by Chen et al. [Journal of Computational Physics, 445, 110624, 2021] from a linear partial differential equation (PDE) to a nonlinear PDE: the 1D Burgers' equation. To strictly impose a discrete approximation of the governing equation, the Burgers' equation is first locally discretised (using a finite difference stencil) then decomposed into a constraint matrix and a prediction matrix. Using tools from linear algebra, the constraint matrix is used to construct a projection matrix. A physics informed neural network (PINN) [Raissi et al. Journal of Computational Physics, 378, 686, 2019] is used to predict the velocity, and a final unlearnable layer projects the velocity prediction to the hyperplane of exact solutions to a discretised form of the Burgers' equation. Our initial results indicate that the HCP-PINN initially trains similarly to an equivalent PINN, and as the PINN loss plateaus, the HCP-PINN loss continues to decline. When tested on a previously unseen uniform grid of points covering the domain, the HCP-PINN exhibits higher accuracy, converging to a data error approximately an order of magnitude lower than the comparable PINN. We also observe that the inclusion of the HCP layer results in better observance of the governing PDE. Our findings suggest that the HCP-PINN can be more robust to the selection of physics collocation points, and less dependent on collocation point quantity.

papers.title: ROOF: Learning Humanoid Fall Recovery under Overhead Constraints
papers.abstract: A fallen humanoid beneath an overhead obstacle faces a coupled recovery problem. It must create clearance while organizing support for a stable rise, since attempting to stand before making room can further increase obstruction. We introduce a reinforcement learning method with contact-supported geometric escape guidance, which rewards incremental reduction of robot-obstacle overlap without prescribing an escape path. To achieve this, a learned motion prior, together with posture-dependent support and joint-stall costs, is proposed to shape a single policy that learns when to clear the obstacle, how to establish support, and when to complete the rise, all using proprioception alone. In simulation, it recovers in 88.5% of trials beneath plates that can only be lifted, compared with 18.9% without geometric guidance, and in 98.6% of trials beneath free plates with randomized size, mass and placement. On a Unitree G1, the deployed policy recovered in 95 of 150 attempts across seven real-world obstacle scenes, including furniture and multi-object arrangements absent from training. papers.title: Cost-Aware Stopping for Freeze-Thaw Bayesian Optimization: When Does One-Step Lookahead Suffice?
papers.abstract: Freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization (BO) evaluates candidates in resumable increments but usually stops at a budget or convergence test. We maximize a budget-free utility, the best observed score minus a cost per increment, with a one-step lookahead: advance the candidate with the largest expected improvement (EI) under a fixed surrogate, and stop once no EI exceeds the cost. This rule, EI stopping, never falls below stopping immediately in expected utility, yet it can stop too early. We construct a certificate, a lower bound on the value of two-step lookahead, that proves such a stop premature, and repeating this correction never lowers expected utility under the surrogate. Under the surrogate, EI stops are premature on average at low costs and lose little at high costs. On three hyperparameter optimization benchmarks, a pre-registered test finds EI stopping noninferior to the correction in most high-cost settings, while the correction gains at low costs on two of the three; more information sharing in the surrogate raises EI stopping's utility. On the surrogates of two published methods, EI stopping trades lower scores for fewer training increments. EI stopping is a simple cost-aware reference whose utility depends on the surrogate.

papers.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting with uncertainty quantification is critical in a variety of scientific applications ranging from epidemiology and economics to energy systems and earth sciences. Yet most forecasting models still need to be developed and trained separately for each domain-specific dataset. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) aim to remove this limitation and enable the application of the same model across domains through large-scale pretraining. However, most existing TSFMs treat each time series independently and therefore cannot model interactions among time series and external drivers. Here, we introduce Chronos-2, a foundation model for zero-shot forecasting that models the interactions between multivariate time series and heterogeneous covariates, which commonly arise in scientific applications. The model infers relationships among time series directly from historical context and generates probabilistic forecasts without task-specific treatment. Across various benchmarks, Chronos-2 achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on average by improving skill scores by 5.2 percentage points relative to the strongest baselines and increasing win rates by 10 percentage points. Chronos-2 is also computationally efficient, generating forecasts for 100 time series in under one second on a single mid-range GPU, 50x and 1000x faster end-to-end than the best task-specific point and probabilistic forecasters, respectively. In addition, we demonstrate its effectiveness in diverse scientific settings -- including infectious-disease forecasting, macroeconomic modeling, carbon-flux prediction, and runoff simulation -- where the model matches or surpasses specialized methods developed for each domain. These results show that a single pretrained model can capture structure shared across temporal systems.

papers.title: Statistical Foundations of Reinforcement Learning: A Non-Asymptotic Perspective
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) embodies a foundational paradigm for sequential decision-making in the face of uncertainty. The rapid growth of model complexity in emerging applications has significantly amplified the challenges of achieving data-efficient RL, particularly in sample-starved scenarios where data collection may be costly, time-consuming, or even high-stakes. Consequently, understanding and improving the data efficiency of RL algorithms has become a central problem of both fundamental theoretical interest and practical importance.   Despite decades of research, the statistical underpinnings of RL remained remarkably underdeveloped until relatively recently, particularly in the finite-sample regimes most relevant to modern practice. Over the past few years, there has been a surge of activity advancing the frontiers of non-asymptotic statistical RL theory, drawing on ideas from high-dimensional statistics and probability, information theory, and statistical learning theory. In this monograph, we present a non-asymptotic treatment for RL based on tabular Markov decision processes, focusing on three canonical sampling mechanisms --- RL with a generative model, online RL, and offline RL --- together with two algorithmic paradigms: model-based and model-free approaches. Centered around non-asymptotic sample complexity analysis, our treatment emphasizes minimax-optimal algorithm design, particularly methods that attain statistical optimality without significant burn-in costs, as well as sharp statistical characterizations of several widely used RL algorithms. Whenever possible, we provide largely self-contained analyses together with intuitive explanations. We also briefly discuss several extensions, such as robust RL, competitive multi-agent RL, federated RL, uncertainty quantification, and RL from human feedback.

papers.title: Online Learning of Heterogeneous Locomotion Dynamics under Reinforcement Learning Policies for Precise Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: How to reuse a pretrained locomotion policy for precise loco-manipulation is still an open problem. We propose an online method to learn the closed-loop dynamics under a frozen locomotion policy. The learned model predicts floating-base motion and improves loco-manipulation accuracy. However, unobserved latent conditions of the policy introduce heterogeneous responses, meaning that the same observed state will lead to different motions. Direct learning without accounting for this heterogeneity introduces bias and fluctuations into dynamics estimates, degrading floating-base prediction and end-effector tracking. To address this problem, a contaminated Gaussian model is proposed to approximate the effects of latent conditions. The model uses two Gaussian components to approximate predictable and unpredictable responses under the same observed state. Then, the contaminated Gaussian model is combined with a Gaussian process to construct an online learner using random Fourier features (RFFs). The learner estimates each response's probability of belonging to the predictable component and uses it to weight online updates, capturing predictable responses while reducing bias and fluctuations caused by heterogeneous observations. With consistent and unbiased dynamics estimates, model predictive control (MPC) predicts floating-base motion accurately and enables precise loco-manipulation. A finite-sample error bound is established to ensure uniform convergence in online learning. Simulation and hardware experiments demonstrate consistent end-effector tracking across different manipulator configurations and tasks, with errors of 0.01 m.

papers.title: Learning Nonlocal Interactions in Large-Scale Heterogeneous Metamaterials through Scientific Machine Learning
papers.abstract: In multiscale systems, nonlocal interactions among spatially distributed constituents can unlock collective, potentially emergent behavior irreducible to individual constituent responses. Beyond characterization, nonlocality in multiscale systems is increasingly viewed as a design element across fracture mechanics, wave physics, and disordered systems. Existing nonlocality theories provide rigorous descriptions and mechanistic insight, but often require prescribed analytic forms, range, symmetries, or periodicity. Machine learning offers a data-driven route to learn interactions, yet principled approaches that tie the network design to physical theory remain nascent. Here we present domain-decomposition attention neural operator (DANO), which learns configuration-dependent interactions in heterogeneous systems governed by linear field equations from field data alone. Through a case study in large-scale optical metasurfaces, we demonstrate DANO's full-field prediction under geometric heterogeneity and across drive conditions, small-to-large domain transfer, and multifunctional inverse design, with learned interactions validated through physics-based interrogation. As an AI-for-Science tool, it supports interaction discovery and scalable, customizable design of nonlocal multiscale systems, including virtual-reality optics.

papers.title: Towards Out-of-Distribution Uncertainty Quantification for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials via Pre-Training
papers.abstract: Informative uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for the practical deployment of machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), as it provides insight into their reliability across chemical space. Although numerous post-hoc uncertainty estimation methods for MLIPs have recently been proposed, most have been trained in low-data regimes, restricting their applicability to narrow domains of interest. Inspired by the emergence of foundational MLIPs, we propose pre-training uncertainty estimators on large, diverse datasets to enable broader applicability. We pre-train several UQ models on large materials science datasets to quantify the uncertainty of different MLIPs, and evaluate their performance on both in-distribution and out-of-domain (OOD) adsorption-energy predictions. We find that pre-trained uncertainty estimators provide viable zero-shot uncertainty estimates across multiple datasets, while fine-tuning consistently yields positive correlations between predicted uncertainty and prediction error, even on the most challenging datasets. These results lay the groundwork for foundational UQ models for MLIPs, ultimately facilitating their deployment in practical settings by providing users with a priori information about model reliability and applicability.

papers.title: Task Vectors Can Be Linearly Decomposed into Interpretable and Controllable Components
papers.abstract: Task Vectors (TVs) provide a compact way to steer large language models, but they are typically treated as atomized directions merely extracted from hidden states, leaving their internal functional structure poorly understood. Motivated by prior work that decomposes in-context learning into Task Recognition (TR) and Task Learning (TL), we ask whether a single TV can likewise be decomposed into functionally meaningful components. We formulate a TR/TL-based decomposition from candidate-label unembeddings, separating each TV into TR, TL, and residual components, and try to optimize the TR and TL coefficients using Bayesian optimization for more effective intervention. We evaluate this formulation across multiple model families, classification tasks, and both instruction- and demonstration-based TVs. Across these settings, TR/TL-based optimization identifies intervention directions that outperform the original TVs. Although optimization over random directions can also improve performance, TR/TL-based search yields more reliable gains, particularly for instruction-based TVs. Moreover, isolated interventions on the decomposed components produce distinct logit-level effects that are consistent with their intended functional roles. Together, these results suggest that TVs are not monolithic steering directions, but can be decomposed into functionally meaningful components that support both interpretation and control.

papers.title: From fleet trajectories to single-cell promises: hierarchically weighted conformal prediction for battery SOH monitoring
papers.abstract: Interval predictions from conformal prediction are usually read as "90% coverage", but on nested battery data that number promises the fleet average, not the individual cell. We measure the gap on 124 public LFP cells under a preregistered three-tier reporting protocol (fleet, batch, cell): pooled coverage looks healthy (0.875-0.906 across splits) while the worst cell is covered 0.1-2% of the time, with exact binomial tests against the nominal level. We then repair part of the gap with a hierarchically weighted conformal engine whose weights consume only side information frozen at prediction time - signature features, batch labels, cycle indices - and never touch residuals. The preregistered repair criterion passes: 10th-percentile cell coverage moves 0.750 to 0.830 (53% of the gap), the worst cell 0.642 to 0.694, with zero deferrals and a flat sensitivity spectrum. What the engine does not repair is localized rather than left open: under protocol drift the frozen weights harm monotonically on the SOH scale (the absolute scale is reported in full), a structural dead end we report instead of tuning away; and repair capacity is bounded by calibration-pool battery diversity, measured on both datasets. On a cross-chemistry external set the calibrated intervals collapse (0.286), while the within-domain skeleton replicates (pooled 0.933, worst cell 0.686). The deliverable is a reporting protocol - three tiers of promise anchored to measured regimes, worst-cell statistics, deferral share - that makes per-cell interval claims auditable before deployment.

papers.title: Interaction-Aware Sampling-Based Motion Planning for Autonomous Surface Vessels in Urban Waterways
papers.abstract: Autonomous surface vessels operating in urban waterways must coordinate with other vessels in confined spaces while complying with traffic regulations, often without knowing their intentions. We present a decentralized motion planner based on model predictive path integral control, a sampling-based model predictive control scheme. The planner jointly computes a trajectory for the ego vessel and a prediction of the trajectories of the other vessels, and therefore accounts for their interaction. Traffic regulations are encoded as discontinuous costs, which the sampling-based formulation admits without a smooth approximation. We evaluate the method in maps taken from real sections of Amsterdam's canals, in encounters between two vessels and in scenarios with four interacting vessels. Across 780 randomized runs the method reaches every goal without collisions or deadlocks, and outperforms an optimization-based planner designed for the same domain, as well as a version of the proposed planner that does not account for the interaction. We further validate the planner on two scaled vessel prototypes in an outdoor environment, where planning and localization run onboard at 10 Hz, and head-on and crossing encounters are resolved without collisions or rule violations.

papers.title: Patch-Based Deep Kernel Learning for Data Assimilation and Bias Correction with Extremely Sparse Observations
papers.abstract: Data Assimilation (DA) reconstructs the state of a spatio-temporal system by combining sensor observations with the output of a numerical model. Since model states are high-dimensional while observations cover only a small fraction of the domain, DA is a challenging large-scale estimation problem, central to weather forecasting and oceanography. Classical variational methods such as 3D-Var rely on a hand-crafted background error covariance that assumes unbiased errors, and therefore cannot capture state-dependent correlations or systematic model biases. Moreover, their cost grows with the size of the domain. Deep learning (DL) methods can perform DA and bias correction (BC) non-linearly, but typically offer limited interpretability and no calibrated uncertainty estimates. We propose a hybrid framework that couples a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a learnable-kernel Gaussian Process (GP) to jointly perform DA and BC from extremely sparse observations. The model is trained end-to-end by maximizing the marginal log-likelihood, learns a data-driven covariance over the whole grid, and provides both the Maximum A Posteriori analysis and its uncertainty by design. A patch-based strategy reduces the $O(N^3)$ training cost of exact GPs over $N$ grid points to $O(N)$ for a fixed patch size. Inference remains exact and only requires solving a linear system whose $O(m^3)$ cost depends on the number of observations $m \ll N$, not on the domain. The learned covariance can also replace the hand-crafted one in 3D-Var, improving its accuracy without changing the variational formulation. Experiments on sea surface temperature and salinity, with both synthetic and real, extremely sparse in-situ observations, show that the framework outperforms 3D-Var, a classical GP and a competing DL model, while reducing inference time by more than 98% with respect to 3D-Var.

papers.title: PDE-Residual-Informed Kriging
papers.abstract: Physics-informed Gaussian process (GP) methods provide a probabilistic framework for PDE solving. Existing approaches incorporate PDE information in different ways: pointwise conditioning uses the governing equation only at finitely many selected locations, globally constrained GPs restrict the admissible functions to satisfy the PDE exactly, and residual-penalized methods control the PDE mismatch over the whole domain through an additional penalty weight. What is still missing is a GP formulation that directly incorporates global PDE-residual information of the entire domain into its covariance structure, while retaining model flexibility and standard GP conditioning without a separate residual-weight parameter. To solve this issue, this study proposes PDE-residual-informed Kriging (PRIK) based on a PDE-residual kernel. The PDE-residual kernel is constructed by equipping a kernel-section space with an inner product defined by the $L^{2}$ inner product of PDE residuals. This construction makes PRIK yield the posterior mean with minimum integrated squared PDE residual. It also provides direct statistical interpretations: the variance-scale estimate equals the normalized PDE-residual energy (i.e., the integrated squared PDE residual of the posterior mean divided by the number of labeled observations), and the profile likelihood balances this residual energy against model complexity. Under the stated regularity and stability conditions, we establish $H^{2}$-quasi-optimality and convergence rates for the posterior mean, together with a nonasymptotic bound for its PDE-residual norm. We further show that the normalized posterior kernel converges to a variational Green-type kernel and derive a uniform nonasymptotic contraction bound for the posterior variance. Numerical studies provide empirical evidence consistent with the theory and demonstrate the PDE-solving capability of PRIK.

papers.title: Direct and indirect operator learning strategies for parametric optimal control problems
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on the use of learning nonlinear operators via Deep Operator Networks (DeepONets) for approximating the solutions of optimal control problems. We study two operator learning strategies, namely, indirect and direct, both based on DeepONets, for parametric families of optimal control problems where the same problem must be solved many times for different initial data, different parameters, different cost function weights, and different bounds defining the set of the admissible controls. In the indirect strategy two DeepONets approximate the solution operators of the state and adjoint systems, and their predictions are used inside iterative projected gradient algorithms for finding the optimal control. In the direct strategy, a single DeepONet approximates the operator that maps directly to the optimal control generated by a reference solver; consequently, a new control is obtained through a single evaluation of the network. In order to analyze the computational cost, the efficiency, the speed and the accuracy of the learning strategies, we consider an optimal control problem related to an ordinary differential system that describes the temporal evolution of the glioblastoma growth subject to therapeutic interventions. For this specific optimal control problem we propose a discretize-then-optimize strategy, based on an implicit-explicit finite difference method, and then, we develop several numerical experiments in order to compare the two DeepONet learning strategies for this problem. The proposed operator learning DeepONet strategies can be adapted to approximate large classes of optimal control problems related to diverse differential systems.

papers.title: AC-SMPC: Differentiable Actor--Critic MPC with State Constraints for Safe and Fast Robot Navigation
papers.abstract: Achieving safe navigation in confined dynamic environments remains a challenging problem, as robots must balance navigation efficiency with safety. Existing actor--critic MPC architectures typically employ differentiable MPC layers, but this way cannot readily accommodate explicit state constraints, making it intractable to involve collision avoidance within learning-based planning. To address this issue, we propose an actor--critic model predictive control framework with state constraints. We first use vertices to represent the robot and obstacles, and half-spaces to represent the workspace. Based on these, the nonlinear robot dynamics is locally linearized and the hyperplane-based collision avoidance constraints are convexified into the differentiable MPC layer, and then the actor exploits closed-loop feedback to adjust the MPC objective parameters that shape local motion behavior, while the critic evaluates long-term task performance. We further relax the convexified constraints with bounded and penalized slack variables to form an elastic quadratic program, accommodating cases where the local constraint approximations cannot be satisfied simultaneously. Simulation tests and experiments, involving dynamic collision avoidance for multi-robot in narrow cases, illustrate the advantages of the proposed framework in adaptively adjusting the learned policy and improving navigation efficiency over existing approaches while maintaining the motion safety.

papers.title: Bayesian PET Reconstruction with Learned Flow Matching Priors via Langevin Sampling
papers.abstract: Image reconstruction for positron emission tomography (PET) is a challenging inverse problem due to its inherent ill-posedness and Poisson counting noise, particularly in low-dose acquisitions. In this work, we introduce a novel Bayesian PET reconstruction framework that leverages a flow-matching generative prior learned from high-quality PET images. By incorporating this prior, we formulate PET reconstruction as a Bayesian inference problem and solve it via latent-space posterior sampling using the unadjusted Langevin algorithm. We evaluate the proposed method through numerical experiments and benchmark it against classical reconstruction methods and state-of-the-art deep learning-based baselines. The proposed method achieves improved reconstruction performance while enabling posterior uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: HandMimicX: Learning Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation via an Object-Centric Policy from Egocentric Videos
papers.abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from human videos remains an open challenge, particularly in the context of transferring a single demonstration into a spatially generalizable robotic skill and maintaining physically plausible human-like interactions. Unlike prior works that emphasize hand-motion imitation, we introduce an object-centric framework for acquiring dexterous skills from egocentric human RGB-D videos. Within our framework, we formulate the reinforcement learning (RL) objective in terms of object motion to decouple the underlying skill from the specific hand trajectory and impose constraints on hand-object interaction states to promote more anatomically natural hand configurations. Extensive experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate that our method enables efficient learning from human videos and generalizable skill transfer across novel spatial configurations.

papers.title: Cross-Embodiment Motion Planning by Coupling Body-Agnostic World Model with Differentiable Ego-Dynamics
papers.abstract: Motion planning in clutter is embodiment-specific: the feasible free space and reachable commands depend on each robot's geometry and dynamics. Existing cross-embodiment policies output normalized commands that disregard these differences, or compensate through per-robot training and distillation. World models can in principle pool cross-embodiment data, yet command-conditioned models bind their latent dynamics to a single action space, while pose-conditioned models omit the mapping from commands to body-specific motion. On flat ground, however, embodiment affects the planner's observations only through the camera ego-motion. This letter proposes Hourglass, an hourglass-shaped architecture that factorizes cross-embodiment motion planning at this interface: a body-agnostic world model and each robot's differentiable ego-dynamics, which map commands to that ego-motion, are coupled only through it. The world model is trained on data pooled across embodiments and camera mounts; each robot's ego-dynamics is a reduced-order template with identified physical parameters. A generalist parameter-conditioned policy is learned once at this junction: each imagined step rolls out the template and then the world model, and imagination training through each robot's template makes the policy body-aware. On seven simulated robots of five locomotion types, the generalist policy outperforms imitation-learning and diffusion-policy baselines on the same world model by 3.8--10.6 percentage points in success rate and matches per-robot specialists without dedicated training, while approaching its parameter-conditioned MPPI teacher within 1.4--2.8 points without an online map. After three minutes of teleoperated driving for identification, the synthetic-data-trained model transfers zero-shot to a real skid-steer robot unseen in training, navigating unseen indoor scenes.

papers.title: Equation informed time reparametrization for physics informed neural networks
papers.abstract: Physics Informed Neural Networks offer a mesh-free approach to solving differential equations, but their application to time-dependent problems remains challenging, particularly when the governing dynamics involve widely different time scales. With collocation points spread uniformly in time, short intervals of rapid change are under resolved. This work introduces an equation informed time reparameterization framework that modifies the temporal coordinate used during PINN training based on the local dynamics of the governing equation. The proposed method follows a two stage procedure. First, a pilot PINN training provides an approximate solution, which is used to linearize the governing differential operator and estimate its local response to small perturbations. These responses are combined into a time-dependent rate function, large where the dynamics are fast, that defines a strictly increasing transformation from physical time to a new computational time coordinate. A second PINN is then trained on the transformed governing equation, with uniformly sampled collocation points in the new coordinate producing a nonuniform distribution in physical time. Different combination rules and spatial reduction strategies are considered. With the cost of the pilot training included, the method reduces the error by a factor of 4 to 29 relative to the best alternative method on the Kachanov Rabotnov creep-damage model near rupture, and by a factor of 5 to 16 relative to every alternative method on the Frank-Kamenetskii equation near blow up.

papers.title: Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification on Simplicial Complexes with Conformalized Simplicial Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Simplicial neural networks (SNNs) are powerful tools for prediction tasks on higher-order relational datasets stored on simplicial complexes (SCs), a higher-order generalization of graphs. However, SNNs usually lack rigorous uncertainty quantification (UQ), limiting their usefulness in high-stakes scenarios. We propose conformalized SNN (CF-SNN), a framework that, given a simplicial-complex entity with m prediction targets, generates prediction sets for all m targets simultaneously. Under mild assumptions, CF-SNN guarantees that, for each target, the prediction set contains the true label with a user-specified nominal coverage probability, and the realized miscoverage proportion across all m targets is guaranteed to remain close to the nominal level with high probability. Extensive experiments across a wide range of SC prediction tasks demonstrate that CF-SNN is a flexible UQ framework that achieves user-specified coverage while producing informative prediction sets of small size.
