papers.title: Spectrally-selective dynamic thermal emission via optical phase engineering
papers.abstract: Maintaining comfortable temperatures for buildings, humans, and devices consumes a substantial portion of global energy, underscoring the urgent need for energy-efficient thermoregulation technologies. Dynamic radiative thermal emitters that can switch between passive cooling and heating modes offer a promising solution, but most existing devices exhibit broadband optical responses, resulting in unwanted parasitic heat exchange and limited performance. Here, we introduce an elegant strategy that uses a dielectric cap to transform broadband metal-insulator transition (MIT) materials into spectrally selective dynamic emitters. This design creates a highly tunable Fabry-Perot cavity, enabling a tailored thermal emission spectrum by engineering the reflected-wave phase profile. Our Fresnel-formalism-based phasor diagram analysis reveals two key routes for realizing high spectral selectivity: a high-index dielectric cap and a low-loss metallic MIT state, which are further validated by Bayesian optimization. Following this principle, we demonstrated a wide-angle spectrally-selective thermoregulator operating in the atmospheric transparency window (8-13 um), where the thermal emittance can be electrically tuned from about 0.2 to 0.9 through reversible copper electrodeposition on a germanium cavity. Furthermore, this strategy can be extended to multispectral electrochromic windows, enabling switching between solar heating and spectrally-selective radiative cooling. Our work establishes a versatile and generalizable paradigm for spectral engineering of dynamic thermal emitters, opening opportunities in energy-efficient buildings, wearable thermal comfort, spacecraft thermoregulation, and multispectral camouflage.

papers.title: Investigation on the laser welding of laser powder-bed fusion (LPBF) fabricated Ti-6Al-4V alloy: Microstructure, defects and mechanical property
papers.abstract: : After years of research, laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) has developed as an additive manufacturing (AM) method with high accuracy, thus has been considerably applied in aircraft component manufacturing. However, since LPBF technology has to be conducted in the inert gas atmosphere with high concentration, the component size is significantly limited by the size of sealed box. Although meter-scaled LPBF equipment is reported to be available, it still challenges in fabricating efficiently. In the present work, laser welding is used to join the LPBF fabricated Ti-6Al-4V alloy thin sheets (2.5 mm thickness). Regarding the grain structure and the inevitable pore defects, the influence of laser power is investigated systematically. The aim is to achieve the welding joint with good mechanical properties which is stronger than the base metal. Obtained results indicated that the improvement of laser power increases the grain size, and promotes the transformation of fine acicular α' martensite to coarse α' martensite, but increases the porosity. Tensile tests showed that the ultimate tensile strength of the laser welding joints achieves 1084.7 MPa when the laser power is 1750 W, in which case the specimen fractured in the base metal rather than the weld zone or the heat-affected zone. The significance of this work is twofold: On one hand, it provides an innovative way for LPBF technology to break through the limitation of as-built component size; and on the other hand, it clarifies how the laser power influences the welding joints in various aspects.

papers.title: A hybrid computational multi-objective optimization framework for direct age hardening of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF)-processed CuCrZr alloy for simultaneous enhancement of strength and electrical conductivity
papers.abstract: : Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF)-fabricated CuCrZr alloy requires post-processing ageing to enhance its mechanical and electrical performance; however, simultaneously improving strength and conductivity remains challenging because of the inherent trade-off between these properties and their competing responses to ageing temperature and time. Identifying a balanced ageing condition through conventional trial-and-error is therefore challenging. In this work, a hybrid computational multi-objective optimization framework integrating Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) was developed to identify Pareto-optimal direct-ageing conditions for LPBF-fabricated CuCrZr alloy. A face-centered central composite Design (FCCD) was employed to investigate ageing temperatures of 460–580 °C and ageing times of 0.5–5 h, followed by the development and statistical validation of regression models using ANOVA. The refined models demonstrated good predictive capability for UTS (R 2 pred = 76.12%) and electrical conductivity (R 2 pred = 88.61%). Direct ageing increased UTS from 310 ± 0.80 MPa in the as-built condition to 470.50 ± 6.36 MPa, while electrical conductivity increased from 24.47 ± 0.65 to 84.50 ± 0.50 % IACS. Prolonged ageing at 460 °C provided a favorable combination of strength, conductivity, and ductility. The validated RSM models were integrated with NSGA-II to generate a set of Pareto-optimal ageing conditions representing different strength–conductivity trade-offs. Two representative solutions were experimentally validated, with prediction errors below 5.2% for both responses. Overall, the proposed hybrid multi-objective optimization framework provides an efficient strategy for identifying balanced direct-ageing conditions within the processing window and can be extended to other additively manufactured precipitation-hardenable alloys requiring simultaneous optimization of competing properties.

papers.title: Anomaly detection in industrial robotics: A novel dataset and benchmark method
papers.abstract: Industrial robotic manipulators enhance manufacturing productivity and safety, but can experience anomalies that disrupt production and compromise safety. The complexity and high variability of modern robotics applications make anomaly detection (AD) particularly challenging. Data-driven semi-supervised approaches are emerging as a promising solution for this task. To overcome the lack of sufficiently rich labeled datasets, models are trained using only normal data, and anomalies are identified by detecting deviations from the normal distribution. To ensure reliable deployment of this technology, it is crucial to design models that are robust against variations in working conditions. At the same time, the availability of public datasets with data from actual systems is fundamental to compare different strategies. In this paper, we introduce Mitsubishi Electric Anomaly Detection (ME-AD), a novel dataset with data capturing real-world, progressively evolving mechanical faults in robotic manipulators during pick-and-place operations. Unlike existing datasets, ME-AD provides authentic sensor data documenting gradual joint degradation up to a mechanical fault during a complete run-to-failure. Furthermore, we propose a Gaussian Process Regression (GPR)-based anomaly detection method that models robot dynamics and employs a novel uncertainty-aware anomaly score to detect anomalies, offering generalization across unseen motion conditions. Our extensive evaluations demonstrate strong anomaly-detection performance and cross-trajectory transfer to out-of-distribution motion profiles and execution speeds.

papers.title: Quantum-Inspired Causal Bayesian Optimization for Complex Adaptive Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract: Complex systems present a difficult optimization setting because interventions alter the mechanisms that generate subsequent observations, performance is only partially observed, resources are constrained, and the operating environment changes over time. Standard black-box optimization can identify favorable settings within an observed regime yet may misrepresent the consequences of deliberate interventions when confounding, feedback, and distributional shifts are present. This paper develops a quantum-inspired causal Bayesian optimization framework (QICBO) integrating a structural causal model, a dynamically updated Bayesian response surrogate, an amplitude-based classical candidate-search mechanism, and a risk-sensitive constrained acquisition rule. The proposed methodology distinguishes predictive associations from identifiable intervention effects, treats graph uncertainty and posterior uncertainty separately, and prioritizes decisions according to expected benefit, resource cost, safety constraints, and information value. A compact nonlinear benchmark, defined by fully disclosed engineering parameters rather than unreported measurements, provides an algebraically checkable solution and an auditable comparison of candidate-selection probabilities. For the specified benchmark, the interior risk-adjusted optimum occurs at an intervention intensity of approximately 0.447, whereas the unconstrained performance-maximizing intensity is 0.750; the difference demonstrates the decision relevance of explicit risk and resource terms, not evidence of superiority over established optimization algorithms. The paper sets out a prospective real-world validation design, including pre-intervention graph assessment, independent calibration, sequential evaluation, distribution-shift tests, and comparisons against causal and noncausal Bayesian baselines. Its principal contribution is a unified, falsifiable mathematical architecture for combining intervention-aware inference, computationally economical candidate exploration, and robust decision selection in adaptive engineered and socio-technical systems. Empirical effectiveness, computational scaling, and any quantum advantage remain open to measurement. Keywords: causal Bayesian optimization; quantum-inspired search; structural causal models; complex adaptive systems; dynamic Bayesian surrogate; sequential interventions; acquisition functions; risk-sensitive control; causal identifiability; amplitude encoding; posterior calibration; distribution shift; constrained decision-making; adaptive experimentation.

papers.title: Integrating Social Studies Learning Models, Media, and Methods to Support 6C Skills: A Systematic Literature Review of Trends, Patterns, and Underexplored Areas
papers.abstract: This study examines trends, integration patterns, and underexplored areas in using social studies learning models, media, and methods to support the six 21st-century skills (6Cs): critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, communication, character, and citizenship, in elementary education. A PRISMA 2020 systematic literature review searched Google Scholar, SINTA, Garuda, DOAJ, ERIC, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and conference proceedings (2016–2026). Fifty articles were analyzed thematically. Problem-Based Learning, Project-Based Learning, Collaborative Learning, Contextual Teaching and Learning, inquiry, discovery learning, and cooperative models were common. These were combined with interactive digital media, including Canva, Wordwall, augmented reality, PowerPoint, and Quizizz, and with methods such as group discussion, social projects, simulation, role-play, and educational games. Critical thinking and communication were most consistently emphasized, while creativity and collaboration were addressed through projects and group activities. Character and citizenship received less explicit and systematic attention. Gaps include simultaneous development of all six skills, long-term evaluation, authentic assessment, equitable access to digital infrastructure, and teachers’ digital and TPACK competencies. In conclusion, the evidence supports aligning active learning models, suitable media, and collaborative-contextual methods with clearly defined skill targets.

papers.title: Escape room virtual como estrategia de gamificación en el aprendizaje activo en nutrición
papers.abstract: Introduction: Higher education in health requires active methodologies that promote meaningful learning and professional skill development. Gamification through virtual escape rooms has been proposed as an innovative strategy to enhance student motivation and engagement. Objective: To evaluate students' perception of the implementation of a virtual escape room as a gamification strategy in active learning in nutrition. Methods: A quantitative, descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted with 50 nutrition students from two cohorts (2024 and 2025). A structured questionnaire assessed usability, disciplinary integration, learning, and teacher support. Descriptive statistics, Student's t-test for independent samples and, for categorical variables, the chi-square or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate, were applied, with a significance level of p < 0.05. Results: The 2025 cohort scored higher across all evaluated dimensions, with statistically significant differences in most items (p < 0.05): usability, active learning (motivation, dynamism, and student engagement), and teacher support. For disciplinary integration, the difference was significant for content application, whereas overall content coverage and digital skills did not reach significance. Conclusions: The virtual escape room is perceived as a favorable gamification strategy to support active learning in nutrition students. Its implementation is associated with greater motivation, content integration, and competency development in health education.

papers.title: Inovação no Ensino Superior: : metodologias ativas na prática pedagógica universitária
papers.abstract: Innovating university education entails a methodological shift suited to a 21st-century university. In this context, active methodologies have emerged as innovative didactic alternatives for teaching and learning in undergraduate programs; they move away from the emphasis on passive, transmission-based instruction to foster active learning, student agency, and autonomy, while positioning the teacher as a pedagogical mediator. This article presents the findings of doctoral research conducted at two academic units of a public university in the Amazon region, located in the municipalities of Humaitá and Itacoatiara. Methodologically, the study employed a mixed-methods (qualitative-quantitative) approach of a basic research nature, with a sample comprising 111 undergraduate faculty members. Data collection involved a structured questionnaire containing both closed-ended and open-ended questions. The main results demonstrated that the use of active methodologies is viewed as an innovation, as it drives a paradigm shift in the epistemology of pedagogical practice—and in the very nature of teaching and learning—that differs from traditional methods. Furthermore, when combined with digital information and communication technologies, these methodologies enhance learning and introduce innovative features to the teaching process.

papers.title: Efforts to Develop the Pedagogical Competence of Islamic Religious Education Teachers
papers.abstract: Pedagogical competence is a crucial skill teachers must possess to effectively manage learning. This study examines pedagogical competence, how learning theories are applied, and the use of technology in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) teaching. The method used was a literature review. The results indicate that pedagogical competence encompasses understanding student characteristics, designing learning, and conducting evaluations. Learning theories, such as behaviorist, cognitive, constructivist, and humanistic, have been shown to help improve Islamic Religious Education (PAI) teaching. For example, behaviorist theory can foster good habits, cognitive theory helps students better understand material, constructivist theory encourages active learning, and humanistic theory helps develop students' overall potential. Furthermore, the use of technology, such as e-learning, can make learning more engaging, interactive, and tailored to students' needs in the digital age. Therefore, Islamic Religious Education (PAI) teachers need to continuously improve their pedagogical competence through training, technology utilization, and teaching strategies tailored to student needs.

papers.title: TacMind: Benchmarking and Modeling Tactile Interaction States for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct observations of contact physics, local geometry, and interaction dynamics, making it a vital source of feedback for contact-rich manipulation. However, existing tactile manipulation studies are often developed and evaluated within specific task settings, making it difficult to systematically compare how tactile information contributes under different interaction conditions. In this work, we develop a benchmark in simulation comprising 128 tasks organized around three complementary evaluation regimes: Precise, Recognition, and Dynamic. The benchmark further includes controlled static and dynamic task variants and 12 perturbation settings for evaluating robustness under changes in visual and physical conditions. These settings motivate studying tactile information as a temporally evolving interaction representation rather than only as an instantaneous observation. We therefore propose an action-conditioned latent predictive world model that integrates tactile history and learns a tactile state through prediction of future tactile latents. Building on this representation, we design a model that conditions action generation on the learned tactile state and uses predicted future tactile information to refine candidate actions through predictive tactile reflection. Experiments on the proposed benchmark show consistent gains from incorporating tactile information across the evaluated regimes. Project Page: https://tacmind-bench.github.io/

papers.title: DEPLOY-RL: Active Boundary Discovery and Conservative Certification for Deployable Reinforcement Learning in Safety-Critical Continuous Processes
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) policies often outperform classical controllers in simulation, yet rarely reach production in safety-critical processes. The barrier is that there is no principled way to answer "Is this policy safe to deploy?" with statistical guarantees. We introduce DEPLOY-RL, a post-training certification framework built on one key insight: deployment certification requires discovering where failures occur (boundary discovery), not measuring how much everywhere (uniform reconstruction). Our contributions: (1) a contract-coupled acquisition function that concentrates sampling on certification-critical boundaries, achieving approximately 2x sample efficiency with a semi-empirical ambiguity reduction bound (domain-calibrated convergence guarantee); (2) conformal risk control providing finite-sample false-go guarantees (<= alpha) under explicit deployment contracts; (3) a three-way decision framework (Deploy/No-Deploy/Abstain) with fail-safe PID/MPC fallback. In simulations on papermaking (industrial digital twin) and Tennessee Eastman (public benchmark), DEPLOY-RL achieves 4.4% false-go rate (vs. 8.6% for the best baseline) while retaining 88.6% policy coverage, the only method achieving <5% false-go with >85% coverage among 14 baselines under our evaluation protocol.

papers.title: RaMMOBO: Random Max-Margin Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) maximizes $M$ expensive black-box objectives with the goal of approximating the Pareto set, whose objective vectors cannot be improved in one component without sacrificing another. A common quality measure is hypervolume, the volume in objective space dominated by these vectors relative to a reference point. Expected hypervolume improvement (EHVI) directly targets this metric and is one-step Bayes-optimal, but its standard computation scales exponentially with $M$, making it prohibitively expensive for many-objective problems. We introduce random max-margin multi-objective Bayesian optimization (RaMMOBO), whose acquisition function lower-bounds EHVI while requiring only linear cost in $M$ to evaluate. RaMMOBO measures the volume of a max-margin box contained in a candidate's hypervolume-improvement region and averages over random reweightings of the objective space, yielding a utility that is strictly Pareto-monotone on hypervolume-improving outcomes. It naturally handles noisy observations and different probabilistic surrogates and supports efficient gradient-based optimization. Across synthetic and real-world benchmarks, RaMMOBO matches or outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with largest gains at higher $M$, with acquisition optimization up to two orders of magnitude faster than qLogNEHVI. Our implementation is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/rammobo.

papers.title: High-fidelity simulation and reduced-order modeling of optical pumping in quantum devices
papers.abstract: Spatially resolved modeling of optically pumped alkali-metal vapors requires the solution of a high-dimensional nonlinear diffusive quantum master equation (DQME) coupled to state-dependent light propagation. We develop a structure-preserving computational framework for this coupled three-dimensional system in the high-pressure limit. The high-fidelity solver combines second-order finite differences, explicit pseudo-time marching, and an exponential-integrator discretization of the light-propagation equation. The scheme preserves the density-matrix trace, while a derived global pseudo-time-step restriction guarantees nonnegative, bound-preserving population updates and frozen-coefficient $1$-norm stability. In the absence of a closed-form solution for the general coupled problem, the solver is verified against complementary analytical reductions, pumping-rate asymptotics, and a light-propagation invariant, all of which are accurately recovered. Tensorized GPU implementation reduces the per-iteration cost by more than two orders of magnitude relative to a single-core CPU. For repeated parameter queries, we further construct an intrusive POD--Galerkin reduced-order model. The quadratic spin-exchange term is treated by an exact nonlinear quadratic expansion, whereas the nonpolynomial and nonlocal optical-pumping term is hyper-reduced using the discrete empirical interpolation method. At out-of-sample parameter points, the reduced model closely reproduces the full-order population and polarization fields while achieving speedup of more than \(7\times10^3\) relative to the single-core CPU full-order solver. The resulting hierarchy connects verified high-fidelity simulation with efficient reduced-order prediction for spatially resolved alkali-metal spin dynamics.

papers.title: Physics-informed operator learning with dual-critic proximal policy optimization for time-sensitive PDE-constrained control: Application to river pollution management
papers.abstract: Physics-informed operator learning offers spatially resolved surrogate prediction with governing-equation guidance but does not alone ensure operationally feasible control. In contrast, reinforcement learning-based methods achieve computational scalability through policies that may exploit simulator artifacts and generalize poorly outside their training regimes. A physics-informed operator learning framework is proposed that integrates deep operator networks with a dual-critic proximal policy optimization architecture for rapid constrained control. The key innovation combines a one-step physics-informed Deep Operator Network surrogate trained by supervised learning and physics-consistency regularization, achieving an untouched test relative L 2 error of 2.21% and a defect-corrected advection-diffusion-reaction root mean square error of 0.7077, with a dual-critic architecture in which an environmental critic learns from simulator feedback while a separate physics-diagnostic critic provides surrogate-derived advection-diffusion-reaction consistency guidance. Comprehensive validation spans simulator fidelity assessment, surrogate accuracy characterization, controller ablations and held-out generalization testing across unseen parameter regimes and operational disturbances. Relative to standard proximal policy optimization, the physics-informed dual-critic controller increased point-time compliance from 94.20% to 94.86%, reduced integrated exceedance by 11.65% and shortened violation duration by 10.85% at statistically comparable treatment effort; hierarchical 95% confidence intervals supported all three safety differences. The physics-informed controller retained improvements across the evaluated out-of-distribution and operational-stress conditions, while the data-only and physics-informed controllers remained statistically comparable. These results support separated environmental and surrogate-derived diagnostic value estimation within the synthetic advection-diffusion-reaction benchmark.

papers.title: Development of a physically informed neural network with an enhanced loss function for MRI signal modelling based on a system of fractional Bloch equations
papers.abstract: The object of the study is the process of modeling the temporal dynamics of the magnetization vector and the corresponding MRI signal in biological tissues using the system of fractal Bloch equations. The problem to be solved was to estimate the unknown parameters of this system from a limited fragment of the measured signal, taking into account the effects of memory and anomalous relaxation, which the classical Bloch model does not reproduce sufficiently fully. A modular principle for constructing the architecture of a fractal physically informed neural network fPINN (fractional Physics-Informed Neural Network) is proposed and the corresponding loss function is formed. It combines a fully connected network with five hidden layers for approximating the components of the magnetization vector and a parametric module for jointly determining physical and fractional parameters. The improved loss function combines the component of matching the predicted MRI signal with the data and the physical component that takes into account the inconsistencies of the Bloch equations with a nonlocal operator. According to the results of the study, the average relative errors of estimation of all parameters do not exceed 4%, and the fractional parameters of the operators are determined most accurately. The ability of the network to physically consistent extrapolate the dynamics of magnetization beyond the measurement interval is confirmed. The results obtained are explained by the combination of available data with the physical limitations of the model and taking into account the dependence of the current state of the system on its previous evolution. A feature of the developed modular principle of the fPINN architecture is the simultaneous optimization of network weights and model parameters, which ensures their estimation without a separate numerical identification procedure. The practical use of the results is possible for the analysis of MRI signals and the study of non-exponential relaxation in structurally heterogeneous tissues in the presence of a measured signal fragment and the correspondence of the processes to the selected model

papers.title: Physics-Informed Stochastic Neural Operators for Climate and Earth-System Prediction
papers.abstract: Abstract: Climate and Earth-system prediction requires simultaneous representation of nonlinear multiscale dynamics, uncertain initial and boundary conditions, incomplete observations, and physical conservation laws. Data-driven forecasting can capture large-scale statistical structure, yet long forecast horizons and rare events expose difficulties associated with physical consistency and calibrated predictive distributions. This paper develops a Physics-Informed Stochastic Neural Operator for Earth-System Prediction (PISNO-Earth), a proposed framework that maps observed spatiotemporal states and forcing fields to distributions of future climate states while explicitly penalizing governing-equation residuals and conservation violations. The methodology integrates a conditional neural operator, stochastic latent forcing, discretization-aware differential operators, and multi-objective estimation of predictive, dynamical and probabilistic losses. It specifies an observation-alignment protocol, temporal and geographic holdouts, ensemble evaluation, and stratified diagnostics for tropical cyclones, heavy precipitation and subseasonal anomalies. A closed-form diffusion problem supplies an independently reproducible numerical benchmark: at a normalized forecast horizon of 0.10, its leading-mode amplitude is approximately 0.3727 relative to the initial amplitude, illustrating how a conservation-compatible decay constraint can be checked without asserting an unmeasured forecasting gain. The proposed architecture makes physical consistency, uncertainty reliability, and resolution transfer jointly testable, rather than treating them as interchangeable performance criteria. The principal contribution is a falsifiable and implementation-oriented modelling specification with explicit ablations, evaluation metrics, and operational safeguards. Large-scale forecasting benefits remain hypotheses until the proposed system is trained and evaluated on independently sourced Earth observations and reanalysis archives. Keywords: neural operators; physics-informed learning; stochastic partial differential equations; climate prediction; Earth-system modelling; Bayesian uncertainty; probabilistic forecasts; conservation constraints; spectral operators; subseasonal prediction; extreme precipitation; ensemble calibration; resolution transfer; causal forcing.

papers.abstract: Introduction . Conclusion . The VITALITYSCOPE platform is a tool for reconciling interests in overcoming quantum-resonant phenomena on planet Earth and extending human life.

papers.abstract: Analysis of recent research and publications. The integration of real–time optimization with model predictive control and data–based hierarchies for beneficiation performance planning have been developed in a number of works; however, the exchange between levels is mostly one–way and does not provide for the propagation of separation–model uncertainty estimates from the operational level to the tactical one. The purpose of the study is to develop a tactical–operational control architecture for iron ore beneficiation processes that combines static multi–criteria Pareto planning by NSGA–II/III with operational distributed model predictive control through a regulated two–way interface and provides end–to–end uncertainty computation from the separation–model level to the daily–planning level. Presentation of the main material. The plant performance planning problem is formalized as a five–criteria Pareto problem (concentrate output, iron content, energy and environmental costs, capacity utilization) for four mineralogical–technological ore varieties over a 30–day horizon. A comparison of NSGA–II and NSGA–III showed that NSGA–II provides wider and more uniform coverage of the Pareto front (normalized hypervolume 0.330, 29% higher than NSGA–III). The separation–model coefficients were calibrated against industrial data from three magnetic separators using block bootstrap. A regulated coordination mechanism is proposed with a forward flow (Pareto set–points and admissible deviation zones computed from confidence intervals) and a backward flow (execution statistics and updated covariance matrices). The upper–level reaction is governed by a three–threshold scheme with a statistically justified upper bound of 30%. A robustness metric of Pareto–front points to separation–parameter identification error is developed. Conclusions. A numerical experiment with a 30–day scenario confirmed the operability of the reaction regulation: after parameter drift and Pareto–front recomputation, the fraction of time outside the admissible zone returns to the normal range. The proposed architecture provides end–to–end uncertainty computation from the separation–model level, through daily–planning operating points, to operational distributed control.

papers.title: INOVASI PEMBELAJARAN PENDIDIKAN AGAMA ISLAM DI SEKOLAH UMUM: KONSEP, BENTUK, DAN STRATEGI OPTIMALISASI
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aims to analyze the concept, forms, supporting factors, inhibiting factors, and optimization strategies of Islamic Religious Education (PAI) learning innovation in public schools in the digital era. The study focuses on understanding how innovation can be developed through curriculum, learning methods, instructional media, and evaluation systems while maintaining Islamic educational values. Methods: This research employed a qualitative descriptive approach using the library research method. Data were collected from scientific journal articles, books, educational regulations, and academic documents related to Islamic Religious Education learning innovation. The literature was obtained through databases such as Scopus, SINTA, Garuda, and Google Scholar, and analyzed using data condensation, data display, conclusion drawing, and source triangulation techniques. Results: The results indicate that PAI learning innovation is not limited to the use of digital technology but involves comprehensive transformation in curriculum development, active learning strategies, adaptive media utilization, and authentic assessment. The implementation of innovation is influenced by teacher competence, infrastructure availability, educational policies, and students’ readiness. Novelty: This study provides comprehensive synthesis of PAI learning innovation by integrating technological aspects with pedagogical and Islamic value dimensions. The findings offer a conceptual framework for developing contextual, meaningful, and character-oriented PAI learning in public schools.

papers.title: องคประกอบสมรรถนะของครในการจดการเรยนรเพอเสรมสรางทกษะชวตและอาชพ ของนกเรยนในโรงเรยนขยายโอกาสทางการศกษา จงหวดสกลนคร
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify the components and behavioral indicators of teachers’ competencies in learning management to enhance life and career skills among students in educational opportunity expansion schools in Sakon Nakhon Province, Thailand. A sequential exploratory mixed-methods approach was employed through three stages: 1) a synthesis of nine documents and research studies, 2) semi-structured interviews with five experts, and 3) an evaluation of the appropriateness and feasibility of the identified components by five experts. The research instruments included a document synthesis form, a semi-structured interview protocol, and a five-point rating scale. Data were analyzed using content analysis, frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations. The findings revealed that seven competency components were initially identified, of which six met the established criteria, comprising 24 behavioral indicators. These components encompassed 1) curriculum integration, 2) active learning management, 3) responsiveness to learner diversity and contextual needs, 4) the provision of safe learning environments, 5) collaboration with parents and communities, and 6) partnerships with career-related networks. Each component comprised four behavioral indicators. Overall, the components were rated at the highest level of appropriateness (M = 4.83, SD = 0.38) and a high level of feasibility (M = 4.17, SD = 0.52). Experiential active learning received the highest appropriateness rating, whereas collaboration with parents, communities, and career-related networks received the lowest feasibility rating, although it remained within the acceptable range. These findings provide a preliminary framework for developing teachers’ competencies in educational opportunity expansion schools, emphasizing community-responsive learning management, support for at-risk students to prevent school dropout, and the integration of authentic learning experiences with career skills and local labor market needs

papers.title: Determining electron-beam melting parameters for Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy slab ingots via numerical simulation of heat and mass transfer processes
papers.abstract: This study investigates conditions that enable the production of high-quality titanium alloy ingots by electron beam melting (EBM). The results from numerical simulation of heat and mass transfer processes are reported, aimed at solving the task of determining the melting regimes of ingot slabs in a continuous crystallizer. Calculations were performed using the finite element numerical method applying the constructed mathematical model of laminar hydrodynamic melt flows and temperature fields in the ingot. The regularities of these processes have been determined. The model makes it possible to determine the geometry of the metal crystallization front taking into account the liquidus-solidus interphase transition zones. The geometry of this front significantly affects the quality of the metal, its uniformity in the volume of the ingot, and the distribution of alloying elements. As a result, a reasonably flat crystallization front was obtained, which meets these conditions. Unlike very expensive full-scale experiments, numerical modeling has made it possible to solve this task and find the necessary parameters for the melting regime by calculation. It was established that heat transfer in the liquid phase of the metal is mainly due to heat and mass transfer due to the movement of the melt and significantly depends on the speed of drawing the ingot, the power of electron beams, and the trajectories of their movement along the surface of the pool. Based on the calculated modes, high-quality ingots-slabs with a cross section of 170 mm × 600 mm from the Ti-6Al-4V alloy were melted at the E. O. Paton Institute of Electric Welding, the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine. The mass speed of drawing the ingot was 250 kg/h, the power of two electron beams was 2 × 54 kW. This alloy is widely used in the aerospace industry

papers.title: Nanocellulose-enabled hydrocolloid inks for 3D food printing: from molecular interactions to sensory performance and sustainability
papers.abstract: Nanocellulose, food-printing rheology, sensory science, and environmental assessment have largely been reviewed separately, leaving formulators without a single evidence base for selecting nanocellulose architecture and hydrocolloid interactions against a target eating experience. This review addresses that gap with a decision-supporting, hypothesis-generating framework linking consumer sensory targets to measurable instrumental proxies, nanocellulose-hydrocolloid architecture, extrusion-based printability, and environmental burden, applying an evidence-tier scheme that separates direct evidence in edible, 3D-printed matrices from evidence extrapolated from non-printing food or non-food systems. Cellulose nanocrystals (CNC), cellulose nanofibrils (CNF), and bacterial nanocellulose (BNC) are compared not by ranking one as universally superior but by the surface chemistry, aspect ratio, and network-forming behavior that suit each to different combinations of printability, sensory target, and production burden. The review synthesizes how these features govern viscosity, yield stress, shear-thinning, storage modulus, and structural recovery, and critically evaluates the evidence linking these descriptors to sensory attributes such as cohesiveness, creaminess, juiciness, and fibrosity, showing this evidence remains dominated by rheology alone rather than paired rheology-tribology-sensory-panel data. Hybrid systems combining nanocellulose with proteins and polysaccharides are examined as a route to improved mechanical strength, mouthfeel, and resemblance to conventional or animal-based foods. Life-cycle evidence for nanocellulose production and printing pathways is synthesized critically, showing that environmental performance depends on process- and system-boundary choices rather than on feedstock renewability alone. Three limitations constrain the underlying literature: rheological values are highly condition-dependent, so no universal printability threshold is yet supported; environmental superiority must be demonstrated on a harmonized basis rather than assumed; and sensory validation still relies on small, non-standardized panels. For formulators, the practical implication is that nanocellulose type and formulation strategy should be selected against the sensory target first, with printing parameters optimized within the resulting formulation space, reducing trial-and-error formulation within a transparent, uncertainty-aware framework that is not yet a validated formulation methodology. Food safety and regulatory status, which depend on nanocellulose source and surface modification, are treated as a gate that applies before any of these design choices.

papers.title: Plantwide control design for highly load-flexible Power-to-X processes: A systematic procedure applied to renewable ammonia production
papers.abstract: Power-to-X processes depend on an intermittent renewable electricity supply and therefore operate continuously across a wide load range rather than at a single design point. Established plantwide control procedures were developed around a single steady state, and existing extensions address bounded turndown, discrete production transitions, or supervisory model predictive control; the design of the regulatory control layer itself for continuous, wide-range, load-flexible operation remains open. We propose a systematic, simulation-based procedure structured in three stages: defining control objectives and constraints across the load range, designing a basic control system using only single-loop proportional-integral controllers, and adding advanced control elements only where validation reveals a specific need. Load flexibility is addressed by identifying every control loop at multiple operating loads, pairing manipulated and controlled variables using a relative gain array aggregated across loads, and tuning from the load-dependent process parameters. We demonstrate the procedure on a high-fidelity, pressure-driven Power-to-Ammonia model of a 500,000 t/yr plant implemented in a commercial process simulator, yielding a regulatory layer of 15 control loops, extended by a feedforward-cascade element for the steam temperature and a ratio-cascade element for the reactor-inlet ratio. The resulting control system operates stably across the full 10%–100% load range at ramping rates of 3%/min, using a single fixed tuning per loop. A decentralized regulatory layer of simple, well-understood controllers is therefore sufficient for highly load-flexible operation of the presented process, and acts as the basis on which scheduling and real-time optimization must subsequently build.

papers.title: Nonlinear mixed-effects modeling of gastrointestinal glucose absorption for Bayesian digital twin identification
papers.abstract: Background Digital twin (DT) methodologies for type 1 diabetes require personalization of physiological models using continuous glucose monitoring and exogenous insulin data. The imbalance between data information content and model complexity often necessitates Bayesian estimation for model identification, requiring informative a priori parameter distributions that are difficult to obtain from the literature, especially for parameters describing gastrointestinal glucose absorption. This study aims to provide such priors by modeling inter-subject variability of meal glucose rate of appearance (Ra). Methods Four glucose absorption models used in published DT were formulated within a nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) framework. Models were identified using Ra derived from gold-standard tracer data collected in 43 adults undergoing either a mixed meal (MTT) or an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). A stepwise, parsimony guided, model-building strategy was adopted to define the random-effects structure and incorporate covariate effects. Parameter estimation was performed using likelihood-based methods. Model adequacy was assessed through parameter precision and visual predictive checks. Results All models achieved adequate fits of Ra with acceptable parameter precision. Test type and body mass index were the covariates explaining most of the inter-subject variability. While all models well reproduced mixed-meal Ra, differences were observed in their representations of OGTT responses. For each model, fixed effects, random-effects covariance matrices, and covariate relationships were estimated, enabling the construction of ready-to-use prior parameter distributions for Bayesian DT implementations. Conclusions The proposed NLME-based framework provides physiologically grounded prior distributions that will support researchers in designing robust and physiologically consistent Bayesian DT algorithms.

papers.title: SPAR-RM: A SECURE PHYSICS-AWARE AND RELIABILITY-AWARE AI FRAMEWORK FOR CYBER-PHYSICAL RESILIENCE AND AUTONOMOUS RECOVERY IN MISSION-CRITICAL ENGINEERING INFRASTRUCTURE
papers.abstract: Mission-critical cyber-physical systems require more than accurate intrusion detection: defensive decisions must distinguish malicious manipulation from equipment faults, quantify physical and reliability consequences, anticipate cascades, and avoid remediation actions that create new hazards. This paper proposes SPAR-RM, a Secure Physics-Aware Resilience and Reliability Management framework that fuses network, controller, process, equipment-health, and digital-twin residual data. A temporal encoder models dynamic behavior, a graph module represents cyber, physical, control, and functional dependencies, and a reliability engine maps anomalies to failure probability, remaining useful life, and service risk. An uncertainty-aware trust monitor and deterministic safety gate govern autonomous recovery. SPAR-RM was evaluated through a hybrid benchmark-and-simulation protocol using 4,377,814 raw observations from SWaT, WADI, HAI, TON_IoT, and an EPANET-based process digital twin, producing 490,000 valid event-grouped temporal windows. Across five independent runs, SPAR-RM achieved 97.1 ± 0.2% accuracy, macro-F1 of 0.966 ± 0.003, MCC of 0.957 ± 0.003, and ROC-AUC of 0.991 ± 0.001. It reduced attack-versus-fault confusion to 2.9%, obtained cascade AUC of 0.982 with 14.3 min mean warning, lowered remaining-useful-life MAE to 4.6%, and raised the Cyber-Physical Resilience Index from 0.638 to 0.930 relative to a conventional IDS. Recovery time fell to 17.5 min and unsafe autonomous actions to 0.3%. These findings demonstrate the operational value of consequence-aware, physics-constrained, reliability-linked inference, while live safety-certified field deployment remains future work.

papers.title: Neuro-Symbolic Quantum Intelligence for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
papers.abstract: Abstract Autonomous scientific discovery requires the coordinated execution of hypothesis generation, evidence appraisal, formal reasoning, experimental selection and uncertainty-aware revision. Contemporary multi-agent systems have begun to connect literature interpretation with laboratory feedback, while neuro-symbolic methods can constrain machine-learned representations with interpretable logical rules. Quantum information processing introduces additional opportunities for structured search and experimental design, but also substantial constraints from device noise, access cost and limited empirical advantage. This paper develops Neuro-Symbolic Quantum Intelligence (NSQI), a proposed architecture that combines neural hypothesis generators, ontology-linked evidence graphs, a convergent symbolic validation layer, resource-bounded quantum or quantum-inspired search, and Bayesian experimental selection. Its mathematical formulation introduces a constrained candidate-scoring rule, density-operator evolution for quantum modules, risk-adjusted expected information gain and a provenance-weighted evidence update. An explicitly assumed numerical scenario demonstrates how the framework ranks three prospective experiment candidates and how a feasibility or safety gate can change the preferred action; these results are analytical consequences of declared inputs rather than observations from a deployed system. A prospective protocol specifies real-source evidence capture, independent verification, matched-compute baselines, reproducibility controls and human oversight. The contribution is a falsifiable integration model that separates logically valid proposals from empirically supported discoveries, permits classical fallback whenever quantum execution is unsuitable and identifies measurable criteria for assessing scientific usefulness. The study advances a testable research design rather than asserting established quantum advantage or laboratory discovery. Keywords: neuro-symbolic artificial intelligence; autonomous scientific discovery; quantum intelligence; ontology-grounded reasoning; Bayesian experimental design; quantum error correction; multi-agent systems; symbolic regression; epistemic uncertainty; active learning; formal verification; evidence provenance; constrained optimization.

papers.title: Mathematically Constrained Generative AI for Multiscale Scientific Simulation
papers.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence offers a route to accelerated scientific simulation, yet unconstrained generation can violate conservation laws, governing differential equations, boundary conditions, and cross-resolution consistency. These failures are consequential when local errors propagate across temporal and spatial scales. This study develops the Multiscale Constraint-Guided Generative Simulation (MCGGS) framework, in which conditional generation is coupled to a differentiable physics residual, invariant-preserving correction, and hierarchical interface agreement. The framework formalizes admissible simulation states as intersections of physical and numerical constraint sets and distinguishes soft penalties from hard projection or operator-based parameterization. A composite optimization objective balances distributional fidelity, partial differential equation residuals, conservation, uncertainty calibration, and cross-scale consistency. To assess mathematical behavior without presenting uncollected observations as empirical evidence, a reproducible one-dimensional periodic diffusion problem supplies a controlled numerical evaluation. An unconstrained perturbed candidate field is compared with a Fourier-Galerkin correction that enforces total mass and mode-consistent decay. Across four evaluation times, the correction reduces reference error and eliminates the imposed mean-state drift, demonstrating in this controlled setting why physically admissible output mechanisms can strengthen simulation reliability. The numerical exercise does not establish performance for a trained generative model or a complex scientific application. The article identifies testable hypotheses, experimental data requirements, solver-based baselines, and verification criteria for extending constrained generation to materials, molecular dynamics, and Earth-system models. The central contribution is an integrated mathematical design and evaluation protocol separating generative expressivity, scientific admissibility, and empirical generalization. Keywords: physics-constrained generative modelling; multiscale simulation; partial differential equations; conservation laws; neural operators; generative priors; Fourier–Galerkin projection; hierarchical consistency; scientific machine learning; uncertainty quantification; inverse design; differential constraints; numerical verification.

papers.title: PSYCHOLOGICAL AND PEDAGOGICAL FOUNDATIONS FOR DEVELOPING THE RESEARCH COMPETENCE OF HIGHER EDUCATION STUDENTS
papers.abstract: The article provides a theoretical analysis of the psychological and pedagogical foundations for developing the research competence of higher education students. The relevance of the study stems from the requirements of higher education standards and the National Qualifications Framework, the digitalization of education, the spread of artificial intelligence tools, and the risk of a formal approach to research tasks. The concepts of research activity, research skills, research culture and research competence are distinguished. Based on a synthesis of scientific approaches, a four-component structure of research competence is substantiated, comprising motivational-value, cognitive, operational-activity and reflective components. Its psychological foundations are identified as cognitive motivation, critical thinking and metacognition, research self-efficacy, learner autonomy and reflection. The pedagogical foundations include the principles of continuity, the unity of teaching and research, student agency and academic integrity, as well as active learning methods, research supervision, responsible use of artificial intelligence and a combination of expert assessment with self-assessment. It has been shown that research-based learning has the greatest developmental potential and that research experience increases students' research self-efficacy. The role of the supervisor as a model of research behavior and the need to teach students transparent and critical use of artificial intelligence are emphasized. A model of continuity in developing research competence at the bachelor's, master's and doctoral levels has been proposed, specifying for each level the aim, key skills, psychological emphases, pedagogical tools and expected outcome. Prospects for empirical verification of the model have been outlined.

papers.abstract: This article discusses the theoretical and practical foundations of the effective use of innovative technologies in the modern education system. The importance of updated educational content, digital educational environments, active learning methods, and modern pedagogical technologies in improving the quality of education is analyzed. In addition, the article describes the features of using information and communication technologies, interactive teaching methods, and criterion-based assessment systems in the educational process. The article also examines issues related to increasing students’ cognitive activity, developing their creative abilities, forming critical thinking skills, and improving independent learning competencies through the use of innovative technologies. Furthermore, the role of teachers’ professional mastery and innovative competence in ensuring quality education is highlighted, and effective ways of organizing the educational process in accordance with modern educational requirements are proposed. The study concludes that the systematic use of innovative technologies in the teaching and learning process contributes to improving students’ knowledge quality, developing their functional literacy, and forming competitive individuals.

papers.title: Quantum-Enhanced Generative Learning for Precision Genomics and Molecular Discovery
papers.abstract: Abstract Precision genomics and molecular discovery require generative systems that connect heterogeneous biological information with functional candidate design while controlling uncertainty, biological risk and computational expenditure. This study develops Quantum-Enhanced Genomic and Molecular Learning (QEGML), a conditional quantum–classical framework integrating a modality-aware encoder, a parameterized quantum latent distribution, a classical molecular or sequence decoder, and constrained candidate selection. The research combines a focused synthesis of relevant literature with mathematical derivation and transparent numerical scenario analysis. No new patient cohort, quantum-hardware experiment or biological assay is reported. Conditional likelihood and distributional regularization define training, while activity, off-target effects, toxicity, resource burden and predictive uncertainty determine selection. A four-candidate calculation shows that the highest assumed activity does not necessarily yield the preferred feasible candidate. With the declared weights, uncertainty adjustment changes the selected candidate from A to B, increasing the evaluated risk-adjusted utility from 0.650 to 0.715. The ranking crossover occurs at a risk-aversion coefficient of 0.1875. Independent-shot calculations further show that reducing the worst-case standard error of a binary measurement from 0.050 to 0.0125 requires increasing the shot count from 100 to 1,600. A published molecular-discovery example is considered separately from these calculations. Comparative analysis specifies matched classical controls, noise ablations and cost-aware evaluation without assigning unmeasured performance gains to the quantum component. The contribution is an auditable framework linking generative representation, decision reliability and experimental accountability. Its practical value remains conditional on prospective biological validation and demonstrable improvement over strong classical alternatives. Keywords: quantum generative learning; precision genomics; multi-omics integration; conditional generation; variational quantum circuits; quantum Born machines; molecular discovery; genomic language models; constrained optimization; uncertainty quantification; finite-shot sampling; model calibration; experimental validation; computational benchmarking.

papers.title: Yaşlı hastada femur boyun kırıkları
papers.abstract: Yaşlı hastada femur boyun kırıkları, artan yaşlı nüfusla birlikte sıklığı giderek artan, yüksek mortalite ve morbiditeyle ilişkili eklem kapsülü içi proksimal femur kırıklarıdır.Femur başı kanlanmasının kırılgan yapısı nedeniyle bu kırıklar kaynamama ve avasküler nekroz açısından yüksek risk taşır.Tedavi kararı, kırığın deplasman derecesi ile hastanın biyolojik yaşı, kemik kalitesi ve fonksiyonel durumu temelinde bireyselleştirilerek alınmalıdır.Deplase olmayan (Garden tip I ve II) kırıklarda, 80 yaş ve altındaki, posterior tilti 20°'nin altında olan hastalarda osteosentez; daha ileri yaşta ya da yüksek posterior tiltli kırıklarda artroplasti seçenekleri düşünülmelidir.Deplase (Garden tip III ve IV) kırıklarda artroplasti standart yaklaşımdır.Çoğu hastada hemiartroplasti yeterli olurken aktif ve biyolojik yaşı genç olan seçilmiş hastalarda total kalça artroplastisi daha iyi fonksiyonel sonuç sağlayabilir.Femoral stem tercihi, özel bir kontrendikasyon olmadığı sürece çimentolu olmalıdır.Cerrahi tedavinin başarısı; mümkün olan en kısa sürede ameliyatın yapılması, etkili ağrı kontrolü, deliryumun önlenmesi, erken mobilizasyon, tromboprofilaksi ve ortogeriatrik yönetimin uygulanmasına bağlıdır.Her yaşlı hastadaki femur boyun kırığı, aynı zamanda osteoporoz tedavisinin başlatılmasıyla bir sekonder kırık önleme fırsatı olarak değerlendirilmelidir.

papers.title: การพฒนารปแบบการจดการเรยนร MAGIC Model เพอสงเสรมทกษะ การคดอยางมวจารณญาณ (Critical Thinking) และผลสมฤทธทาง การเรยน เรอง ตรรกศาสตร สำหรบนกเรยนชนมธยมศกษาปท 4
papers.abstract: This research aimed to: 1) compare students’ learning achievement before and after learning through the MAGIC Model; 2) investigate the efficiency of the “Logic Treasure Hunt” board game in enhancing critical thinking skills; and 3) evaluate the suitability of the MAGIC Model for promoting critical thinking skills and learning achievement in Logic among tenth-grade students. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach. The sample consisted of 36 tenth-grade students from Suankularb Wittayalai Rangsit School enrolled in the first semester of the 2025 academic year and 40 mathematics teachers from 40 schools who participated in evaluating the model. Research instruments included MAGIC Model lesson plans, the “Logic Treasure Hunt” board game, a critical thinking skills test, a learning achievement test, and a model evaluation form. Data were analyzed using mean, standard deviation, E1/E2 efficiency index, and dependent samples t-test. The findings indicated that: 1) students’ critical thinking skills after the intervention were significantly higher than those before learning at the .05 level; 2) students’ learning achievement after learning through the MAGIC Model was significantly higher than their pre-learning achievement at the .05 level; 3) the “Logic Treasure Hunt” board game achieved an efficiency level of 81.81/80.06, exceeding the established criterion of 80/80; and 4) the overall suitability of the MAGIC Model was rated at the highest level (x̄ = 4.78, S.D. = 0.31). The findings suggest that the MAGIC Model serves as an effective pedagogical innovation integrating Active Learning, Game-Based Learning, and Constructivist Learning principles to enhance critical thinking skills and improve learning achievement in Logic. The model was highly endorsed by participating teachers and demonstrated strong potential for fostering essential 21st-century competencies among upper secondary school students. Therefore, it can be effectively implemented and adapted for mathematics instruction in diverse educational contexts.

papers.title: Dynamic modeling, efficiency analysis, and hierarchical control of industrial airborne pulp dryers
papers.abstract: Industrial airborne pulp drying is governed by strongly coupled moisture transport, heat transfer, psychrometric behavior, airflow distribution, pressure dynamics, and fan operation. A nonlinear multi-zone dynamic model was formulated to represent these interactions through coupled mass and energy balances, pressure-driven deck-to-deck airflow, centrifugal-fan dynamics, and through-thickness moisture and temperature transport. Overall and thermal efficiencies, specific energy consumption, and specific moisture evaporation ratio (SMER) were incorporated for energetic assessment. A hierarchical direct synthesis methodology (DSM), comprising moisture•temperature and airflow•fan speed cascade loops with chamber-pressure regulation, was evaluated against proportionalintegral-derivative (PID) control and model predictive control (MPC) benchmarks. The MATLAB simulations of a six-zone dryer predicted progressive moisture reduction toward 0.120 kg H2O/kg dry pulp, overall efficiency near 0.60, thermal efficiency near 0.61, and SMER of approximately 0.95-0.96 kg H2O/kWh. The DSM provided the lowest accumulated moisture-tracking error and smooth control action, while PID control gave comparable fast loop regulation. The current MPC implementation exhibited poorer moisture•thermal tracking, indicating the need for further predictive model refinement and systematic tuning. The formulation provides a controloriented basis for subsequent parameter identification and industrial validation.

papers.title: Reviving historical moments: The implementation of role-playing drama in the process of learning history at the higher education level
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine students' perceptions and experiences regarding the use of the drama role-playing method as an active learning strategy in higher education history instruction. Although previous research has explored active learning, there is a research gap regarding how dramatic role-playing facilitates the reconciliation of emotional-affective understanding and cognitive-historical analysis within the complex context of the subject matter of colonialism. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, data were collected from 30 students of the Social Studies Education Study Program at UIN Maulana Malik Ibrahim Malang via an open-ended Google Forms questionnaire consisting of 10 in-depth questions. The data were analyzed using Structured Thematic Analysis with a three-stage coding procedure (open, axial, and selective coding). Research findings indicate that role-playing drama significantly enhances students' conceptual understanding, long-term memory, empathetic emotions, and collaborative skills. However, obstacles such as limited rehearsal time, awkwardness in acting, and the need for a precise narrative script pose major challenges. This study concludes that dramatic role-playing is effective in grounding abstract historical narratives into an immersive learning experience, provided it is supported by structured facilitation from the lecturer.

papers.title: Dual Actor DDPG for Airborne STAR-RIS assisted communications
papers.abstract: This study departs from the prevailing assumption of independent Transmission and Reflection Coefficients (TRC) in Airborne Simultaneous Transmit and Reflect Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (STAR-RIS) research. Instead, we explore a novel multi-user downlink communication system that leverages a UAV-mounted STAR-RIS (Aerial-STAR) incorporating a coupled TRC phase shift model. Our key contributions include formulating a weighted multi-objective optimization problem that jointly optimizes UAV trajectory, active beamforming vectors at the base station, and passive RIS TRCs to maximize fair user throughput while minimizing energy consumption, subject to coupled phase-shift, QoS, and UAV mobility constraints. We design the TRC as a combination of discrete and continuous actions, and propose a novel Dual Actor Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DA-DDPG) algorithm. The algorithm relies on two separate actor networks for high-dimensional hybrid action space. We also propose a novel harmonic mean index (HFI)-based reward function to ensure communication fairness amongst users. For comprehensive analysis, we study the impact of RIS size on UAV aerodynamics showing that it increases drag and energy demand. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DA-DDPG algorithm outperforms conventional DDPG and DQN-based solutions by 24% and 97%, respectively, in accumulated reward. Three-dimensional UAV trajectory optimization achieves 28% higher communication efficiency compared to two-dimensional and altitude optimization. The HFI based reward function provides 41% lower QoS denial rates as compared to other benchmarks. The mobile Aerial-STAR system shows superior performance over fixed deployed counterparts, with the coupled phase STAR-RIS outperforming dual Transmit/Reflect RIS and conventional RIS setups. These findings highlight the potential of Aerial-STAR systems and the effectiveness of our proposed DA-DDPG approach in optimizing their performance.
